C999-CH1.title: Our vibration sensors on wind turbine gearboxes raise false alarms in cold weather.
C999-CH1.text:
Our vibration sensors on wind turbine gearboxes raise false alarms in cold weather.

We tried fixed thresholds per season, but bearing faults are still missed in winter. We have two years of labelled vibration data from 40 turbines.

R0045.title: Bogdan Bajić
R0045.text:
Bogdan Bajić (R0045): Assistant Professor, Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mechanical Engineering; Electrical and Electronic Engineering; Signal Processing; Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.
Keywords: condition monitoring; predictive maintenance; rotating machinery; vibration analysis; bearing fault detection; time-frequency analysis; embedded systems; fault classification; gearbox diagnostics; feature extraction.
Bio: Bogdan Bajić received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Mechatronics Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2012, respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a thesis on vibration-based bearing fault detection using embedded signal processing. He was a postdoctoral researcher at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Ljubljana, from 2018 to 2020, before returning to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor. His group focuses on condition monitoring of rotating machinery — bearings, gearboxes, and electric motors — through accelerometer arrays, time-frequency analysis, and machine learning classifiers running on low-power microcontrollers. He teaches undergraduate courses in Sensors and Measurement Systems and graduate courses in Predictive Maintenance. The laboratory operates a dedicated rotating machinery fault-simulation test rig, a multi-channel vibration data acquisition system, and a set of single-board embedded platforms for on-edge inference.
Open to: contract research; joint projects; consulting; equipment access; student internships; industrial PhD supervision.
Industry experience: During the SensiDrive project, Bajić collaborated with a medium-sized food processing company in Novi Sad to conduct a 14-month field trial of the wireless sensor nodes, including on-site installation, calibration, and follow-up fault confirmation with maintenance staff.
Notes: Bajić has a working test rig and multi-channel DAQ system available for industry-funded experiments; short-turnaround measurement campaigns are feasible. He is particularly interested in companies with rotating machinery maintenance problems where data collection can be done on-site.

R0510.title: Olivera Ognjanov
R0510.text:
Olivera Ognjanov (R0510): Assistant Professor, Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mechanical Engineering; Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnostics; Vibration Signal Processing; Computational Dynamics.
Keywords: planetary gearbox; gear-mesh frequency; torsional dynamics; pitting detection; vibration signal processing; multi-body simulation; harmonic extraction; rotating machinery diagnostics; surface fatigue; spectral analysis.
Bio: Olivera Ognjanov received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Mechanical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2008 and 2011 respectively, and completed her Ph.D. at the same institution in 2017, with a dissertation on torsional vibration decomposition in planetary gearboxes under variable load conditions. She joined the Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation as a teaching assistant in 2012 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2018. Her research group focuses on vibration signal processing for rotating machinery health monitoring, with particular emphasis on gear-mesh frequency harmonic extraction, multi-body torsional dynamics modelling, and early detection of surface fatigue in planetary gearbox stages. She teaches courses in machine dynamics and condition monitoring. The group operates a dedicated gearbox test rig equipped with torque sensors, incremental encoders, and a 24-channel NI data acquisition system.
Open to: joint projects with companies monitoring gearboxes in conveyor, wind, or industrial drive applications; contract research on gear fault detection algorithm development and validation; access to gearbox test rig and NI data acquisition equipment for measurements; student internships in signal processing and experimental vibration measurement; consulting on selection and calibration of diagnostic indices for planetary drive applications; industrial PhD supervision co-funded by industry partner.
Industry experience: Ognjanov collaborated with Konvejer Tehnika d.o.o. (Novi Sad) on a six-month measurement campaign on in-service conveyor gearboxes as part of the PLANETMON project. She has provided informal consulting to two local machine builders on sensor placement and threshold selection for vibration monitoring systems.
Notes: Ognjanov's test rig is booked heavily during the academic year but is more accessible in July and August. She is specifically interested in companies at NTP Novi Sad working on industrial IoT or predictive maintenance platforms that could serve as deployment targets for the embedded monitoring unit developed under PLANETMON. She prefers collaborations where the company provides access to field gearboxes or operational data rather than purely funding-only arrangements.

R0737.title: Gordana Kuzmanović
R0737.text:
Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737): Senior Research Associate, Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics), Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mechanical Engineering; Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnostics; Machine Learning Applied to Engineering; Signal Processing.
Keywords: vibration analysis; rotating machinery; bearing fault diagnosis; gear fault detection; frequency-domain feature extraction; physics-informed machine learning; envelope spectrum; cyclostationary analysis; multi-class fault classification; drivetrain condition monitoring.
Bio: Gordana Kuzmanović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Mechanical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2003 and 2006 respectively, and completed her Ph.D. at the same institution in 2012 with a dissertation on frequency-domain fault indicators for rolling-element bearings under variable speed conditions. She has been a Senior Research Associate in the Department of Machine Design and Mechanics since 2018. Her group focuses on vibration-based condition monitoring of rotating machinery, combining signal processing techniques—envelope analysis, cepstral pre-whitening, cyclostationary decomposition—with physics-informed machine learning models for multi-class fault classification. She teaches courses in Machine Dynamics and Applied Vibration Analysis at both undergraduate and master's level. Laboratory work is conducted in the FTS Rotating Machinery Diagnostics Lab, equipped with a modular drivetrain test rig, multi-axis accelerometers, laser tachometry, and a data acquisition system capable of 200 kS/s per channel.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing condition monitoring products or services; contract research on vibration-based fault detection for specific machine types; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed at NTP Novi Sad companies; student internships in the Rotating Machinery Diagnostics Lab; consulting on sensor placement, feature extraction pipeline design, and classifier validation; equipment access to the modular drivetrain test rig for company-sponsored experiments.
Industry experience: During the WINDMON project Kuzmanović worked directly with a turbine operator in Vojvodina to install and calibrate field monitoring hardware and interpret alarm events over two years of operation. She has also provided informal technical advice to a Novi Sad-based maintenance services firm on vibration acceptance criteria for overhauled gearboxes.
Notes: Kuzmanović is particularly interested in collaborations where access to proprietary field vibration data can complement her laboratory datasets; she is prepared to sign standard NDAs. Her benchmark dataset paper is under review and expected to increase interest from algorithm developers seeking a validated testbed.

R0738.title: Igor Starčević
R0738.text:
Igor Starčević (R0738): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Machine Learning and Data Mining; Industrial Control and SCADA Systems; Predictive Maintenance and Condition Monitoring; Renewable Energy Systems.
Keywords: anomaly detection; predictive maintenance; time-series classification; SCADA telemetry; performance ratio; soiling estimation; photovoltaic systems; fault detection; regression modelling; distributed energy assets.
Bio: Igor Starčević received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2012 respectively, and his Ph.D. in Technical Sciences from the same institution in 2018, with a dissertation on regression-based fault indicators for photovoltaic SCADA telemetry. He joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as a teaching assistant in 2013 and was appointed Assistant Professor in 2019. His group focuses on time-series anomaly detection, predictive maintenance pipelines, and performance degradation modelling for distributed energy assets including solar parks, small wind installations, and district heating substations. He teaches courses in machine learning and industrial data systems. The group regularly works with real SCADA datasets and uses a GPU-equipped workstation cluster and the university's HIL (hardware-in-the-loop) test bench for validation experiments.
Open to: joint projects with companies operating PV parks, wind farms, or district heating networks that can provide SCADA data access; contract research on anomaly detection pipeline development and validation; industrial PhD co-supervision with companies in the energy or industrial IoT sector; student internships focused on data engineering and model deployment tasks; consulting on threshold selection, sensor quality assessment, and maintenance scheduling frameworks.
Industry experience: Starčević provided a six-month consultancy to a regional solar asset management company in 2022–2023, assisting with the specification and partial implementation of an automated performance reporting system based on methods developed in the DIASOLAR project.
Notes: He has an active doctoral student finishing in late 2026, so capacity for new project coordination is limited until 2027; work package participation or contract research roles are more feasible in the near term. He has expressed a preference for collaborations that include data sharing agreements, as access to labelled fault telemetry from new asset types remains the main bottleneck for his group's research.

R0773.title: Branislava Ostojić
R0773.text:
Branislava Ostojić (R0773): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Statistical Process Control; Machine Learning; Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems; Time Series Analysis.
Keywords: multivariate statistical process control; change-point detection; non-stationary time series; adaptive thresholding; unsupervised anomaly detection; cyber-physical systems; online learning; control charts; kernel methods; industrial monitoring.
Bio: Branislava Ostojić received her Dipl.Ing. in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2000, followed by an M.Sc. in 2003 and a Ph.D. in 2009, both from the same institution. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2010, Associate Professor in 2016, and Full Professor in 2022. Her research group focuses on statistical process control for industrial systems, combining multivariate time-series analysis with machine learning methods such as kernel-based change-point detection, online anomaly scoring, and adaptive control-chart thresholds for non-stationary signals. She teaches courses in Stochastic Systems, Applied Statistics for Engineers, and Industrial Data Analysis. The group operates within the Laboratory for Intelligent Measurement and Control Systems at FTN, using a real-time data acquisition testbed with programmable logic controllers, vibration sensors, and a shared high-memory compute server for streaming-data experiments.
Open to: joint research projects with companies operating sensor-instrumented production equipment; contract research on anomaly detection and SPC system design; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed in manufacturing or automation companies; consulting on deployment and calibration of statistical monitoring systems; student internships focused on data collection and algorithm prototyping; equipment access (laboratory testbed with PLC, vibration, pressure, and temperature acquisition).
Industry experience: Ostojić has carried out paid consultancy engagements for two manufacturers in the Vojvodina region, advising on the replacement of rule-based alarm systems with data-driven SPC methods and on the design of operator dashboards for process monitoring. Both engagements ran for approximately six months each.
Notes: Ostojić is particularly interested in collaborators who can provide access to labelled or time-stamped operational data from real production systems, as clean annotated industrial datasets are the main bottleneck for her group's current research. She is not in a position to take on projects requiring extensive hardware integration or embedded firmware development beyond lightweight deployment of pre-trained models.

R0822.title: Vladana Radić
R0822.text:
Vladana Radić (R0822): Full Professor, Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Condition Monitoring and Predictive Maintenance; Signal Processing and Time-Series Analysis; Mechatronics and Rotating Machinery; Machine Learning for Industrial Applications.
Keywords: predictive maintenance; vibration analysis; thermal signatures; rotating machinery; remaining useful life; fault prognosis; multivariate time-series; gearbox diagnostics; infrared thermography; bearing fault detection.
Bio: Vladana Radić received her Dipl.Ing. and M.Sc. degrees in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2001 and 2005, respectively, and her Ph.D. in Mechatronics from the same institution in 2010. She joined the Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation at the Faculty of Technical Sciences in 2010 as an Assistant Professor and was promoted to Full Professor in 2021. Her research group focuses on condition monitoring of rotating machinery—pumps, compressors, gearboxes, and electric motors—using synchronized acquisition of vibration and thermal data, multivariate statistical process control, and data-driven fault prognosis including remaining useful life estimation. She teaches courses in machine diagnostics, signal processing, and industrial automation. The group operates a dedicated rotating machinery test laboratory equipped with vibration measurement rigs, infrared thermography systems, and a multi-channel DAQ infrastructure.
Open to: joint projects with companies in process industries (pumps, compressors, conveyors); contract research for condition monitoring system development and validation; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed at NTP Novi Sad companies; consulting on predictive maintenance system design and sensor selection; equipment access to rotating machinery test rigs and infrared thermography systems; student internships related to data collection and analysis for condition monitoring.
Industry experience: Prof. Radić has collaborated with two Vojvodina-based industrial companies (grain handling and conveyor operations) as project partner and has provided technical consulting to a domestic manufacturer of centrifugal pumps on vibration acceptance testing procedures.
Notes: Prof. Radić is currently supervising three doctoral students and is co-supervising one additional student jointly with Politehnica University of Timișoara; she has limited capacity for new full-time project commitments before mid-2025 but is available for smaller consulting engagements and equipment-sharing arrangements. She prefers collaborations where measurement data can be shared for academic publication.

SYN-PAT-017.title: Adaptive Threshold Vibration Monitoring Node with Dual-Mode Sampling for Rotating Machinery
SYN-PAT-017.text:
Adaptive Threshold Vibration Monitoring Node with Dual-Mode Sampling for Rotating Machinery (2023, granted).
Inventors: Bogdan Bajić (R0045).
A wireless sensor node for continuous bearing condition monitoring comprises a triaxial MEMS accelerometer, a low-power microcontroller, and a sub-GHz radio transceiver. The node operates in a low-power survey mode at reduced sampling frequency and switches autonomously to a high-rate diagnostic mode when an on-chip RMS estimator exceeds an adaptive threshold. The threshold adapts to baseline vibration level over a configurable initialisation window, reducing false triggers caused by operating-point changes. Patent covers the threshold adaptation algorithm, the dual-mode state machine firmware architecture, and the hardware layout of the sensor node enclosure.

SYN-PAT-045.title: Method and Device for Adaptive Threshold Setting in Vibration-Based Bearing Condition Monitoring Under Variable Operating Speed
SYN-PAT-045.text:
Method and Device for Adaptive Threshold Setting in Vibration-Based Bearing Condition Monitoring Under Variable Operating Speed (2020, granted).
Inventors: Vladana Radić (R0822).
The invention describes a method for automatically adjusting alarm and warning thresholds for vibration-derived health indicators—specifically RMS and kurtosis computed in selectable frequency bands—as a function of measured shaft rotational speed sampled from a tachometer signal. A lookup table of baseline healthy-condition feature distributions, indexed by speed bin, is updated online using an exponentially weighted moving average. Threshold levels are recomputed at each measurement interval as multiples of the current baseline standard deviation. The associated device comprises a signal conditioning unit, a microcontroller executing the threshold adaptation algorithm, and a relay output for maintenance alert signalling. The method reduces false alarm rates under variable-speed operation by approximately 60% relative to fixed-threshold implementations in validation tests.

SYN-PRJ-0203.title: Embedded Sensor Intelligence for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Drive Systems
SYN-PRJ-0203.text:
SensiDrive: Embedded Sensor Intelligence for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Drive Systems (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0045 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia; Institute for Automation and Control, Novi Sad, Serbia.
SensiDrive addressed the gap between laboratory bearing-fault research and deployable embedded diagnostic hardware. The project developed a complete pipeline from data acquisition — using both piezoelectric and MEMS accelerometers — through on-chip feature extraction and compressed neural network inference, to wireless condition reporting. A test rig simulating a three-bearing drive shaft was designed and built at FTN Novi Sad. Algorithms were validated on the rig under controlled fault conditions and in a limited field trial at a partner manufacturing facility. The project produced open benchmark data, embedded firmware, and two peer-reviewed publications. A total of four researchers and two graduate students were involved over the project duration.

SYN-PRJ-0240.title: Warehouse Pose Estimation Under Real-World Conditions for Worker Safety Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0240.text:
WARPEST: Warehouse Pose Estimation Under Real-World Conditions for Worker Safety Monitoring (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0575 principal investigator; R0773 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; LogiTrans d.o.o., Novi Sad; VojaDistrib d.o.o., Zrenjanin.
The project developed and validated monocular pose estimation methods adapted to logistics warehouse environments where occlusion, mixed artificial lighting, and heavy machinery create severe domain shift from standard benchmark conditions. Research activities included collection and annotation of the WarePose dataset, design of source-free adaptation procedures, and integration of kinematic constraint layers into detection pipelines. Collaboration with two logistics companies in Vojvodina provided access to real facilities for data collection and for pilot deployment of a software monitoring prototype. The project also supported two PhD students and produced six peer-reviewed publications. The resulting software prototype estimates ergonomic risk indicators from monocular CCTV footage without modifying existing camera infrastructure.

SYN-PRJ-0312.title: Cross-Border Predictive Maintenance Frameworks for Distributed Renewable Energy Infrastructure
SYN-PRJ-0312.text:
MAINTAIN-IPA: Cross-Border Predictive Maintenance Frameworks for Distributed Renewable Energy Infrastructure (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0738 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs; SunField Energy Kft., Kecskemét; Vojvodina Renewables d.o.o., Novi Sad.
MAINTAIN-IPA is a cross-border cooperation project addressing the fragmented and predominantly reactive maintenance practices applied to small and medium renewable energy installations on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. Igor Starčević leads the work package on data integration and machine learning pipeline development, which involves aligning heterogeneous SCADA data from Hungarian and Serbian partners into a common schema and training shared predictive maintenance models. The project includes a pilot deployment at two sites—one wind farm in Bács-Kiskun county and one PV park in the Vojvodina region—with live anomaly alerting integrated into each operator's existing SCADA dashboard.

SYN-PRJ-0428.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Multi-Fault Diagnosis in Industrial Drivetrains
SYN-PRJ-0428.text:
DRIVETRAIN-DX: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Multi-Fault Diagnosis in Industrial Drivetrains (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0737 principal investigator; R0525 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania.
The project develops fault diagnosis methods for industrial gearboxes and rolling-element bearings that incorporate physical knowledge of machine kinematics directly into the structure of machine learning classifiers and feature spaces. Work covers three threads: (1) physics-constrained feature engineering for SVM and RF classifiers, (2) domain adaptation strategies enabling classifiers trained on laboratory rigs to transfer to field machines, and (3) construction and publication of a labelled benchmark dataset from the FTS drivetrain test rig. The project supports two doctoral students and involves a collaboration with Politehnica University of Timișoara. All software and datasets are released openly at project end.

SYN-PRJ-0429.title: Low-Cost Condition Monitoring Systems for Small and Medium Wind Turbines in the Western Balkans
SYN-PRJ-0429.text:
WINDMON: Low-Cost Condition Monitoring Systems for Small and Medium Wind Turbines in the Western Balkans (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2018–2020).
Participants: R0737 work package leader; R0786 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Bay Zoltán Applied Research Institute, Miskolc, Hungary; Vojvodina Renewable Energy Agency, Novi Sad, Serbia.
This cross-border project addressed the lack of affordable condition monitoring infrastructure for the small and medium wind turbine fleet in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Gordana Kuzmanović led the work package responsible for vibration signal processing algorithms and alarm logic, adapting laboratory-developed spectral trending methods to operate on low-cost single-board computers with intermittent connectivity. Field installations on three turbines in Vojvodina provided long-term measurement data used to validate alarm thresholds. The project produced a hardware–software monitoring prototype and a deployment guide for turbine operators, and supported two master's thesis projects at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

SYN-PRJ-0441.title: Fusion of Vibration and Infrared Thermography Data for Condition Assessment of Slow-Speed Industrial Machinery
SYN-PRJ-0441.text:
THERMOVIB: Fusion of Vibration and Infrared Thermography Data for Condition Assessment of Slow-Speed Industrial Machinery (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2018–2020).
Participants: R0822 principal investigator; R0615 team member.
Partners: Žitopromet Vojvodina d.o.o., Zrenjanin, Serbia; Lučka Uprava Novi Sad, Serbia.
THERMOVIB addressed the diagnostic gap for machinery operating at shaft speeds below 100 rpm, where standard vibration-based fault indicators are unreliable. The project developed synchronised data acquisition protocols combining piezoelectric accelerometers and thermal cameras, and constructed fusion algorithms that exploited the complementary sensitivity of each modality to different fault types and severity levels. Field experiments were conducted at a grain handling facility and a river port conveyor installation in the Vojvodina region. The project delivered sensor placement guidelines, fusion algorithm code, and a practical handbook for maintenance engineers working with slow-speed conveyor and elevator machinery. Two master's theses and one conference paper resulted from the project.

SYN-PRJ-0671.title: Interoperable Monitoring Middleware for Industrial IoT with Embedded Statistical Quality Control
SYN-PRJ-0671.text:
IIoTMON: Interoperable Monitoring Middleware for Industrial IoT with Embedded Statistical Quality Control (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0773 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Information Technology and Bionics, Pázmány Péter Catholic University, Budapest; Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica; Chamber of Industry and Commerce Bács-Kiskun County, Kecskemét.
This cross-border project addressed the integration of statistical process control logic into IoT middleware platforms used by small and medium-sized manufacturers in the Hungary–Serbia border region. The Novi Sad team led the work package on SPC algorithm design and embedded deployment, contributing drift-robust anomaly scoring modules certified to run on Cortex-M class microcontrollers. The Hungarian partner coordinated middleware architecture and communication protocols, while a regional chamber of commerce facilitated access to pilot companies. Three pilot deployments were completed: a food-packaging line, a metal-pressing workshop, and a grain-drying facility. Evaluation covered detection latency, energy consumption, and false-alarm frequency over 12-month monitoring periods.

SYN-PRJ-0818.title: Physics-informed monitoring of planetary gearboxes for industrial conveyor and wind energy applications
SYN-PRJ-0818.text:
PLANETMON: Physics-informed monitoring of planetary gearboxes for industrial conveyor and wind energy applications (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0510 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade; Konvejer Tehnika d.o.o., Novi Sad.
The project develops and validates a monitoring framework that combines multi-body torsional dynamics models with vibration signal processing to detect early-stage surface pitting in planetary gearboxes used in conveyor drives and small wind turbines. The core activities include constructing a parameterised simulation library covering gearbox ratios and planet counts common in Serbian industry, performing accelerated fatigue experiments on two physical gearboxes, and deriving operating-condition-aware detection thresholds from the combined simulation and experimental database. A prototype embedded monitoring unit is being developed for field validation at an industrial partner site. The project involves three research groups from the University of Novi Sad and one from the University of Belgrade.

SYN-PUB-00312.title: Gear diagnostics in planetary drives: signal processing and simulation methods
SYN-PUB-00312.text:
Gear diagnostics in planetary drives: signal processing and simulation methods (2022, book chapter, Handbook of Rotating Machinery Condition Monitoring, TechPress Verlag, Stuttgart).
Authors: Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Dušan Tošić (R0174); Velimir Mladenović (R0026); Miroslav Kolar (outside co-author); Goran Lazić (outside co-author).
Keywords: planetary gearbox diagnostics; synchronous averaging; order tracking; cepstrum; failure modes.
This book chapter reviews the signal processing and computational simulation approaches used for diagnostics in planetary gearboxes, covering synchronous averaging, cepstrum analysis, time-frequency methods, and multi-body torsional dynamics modelling. The chapter discusses the practical challenges of sensor placement on rotating carriers, reference signal acquisition for order tracking, and the selection of appropriate diagnostic indices for different failure modes including pitting, spalling, and tooth fracture. Example results from laboratory gearbox experiments at two test facilities are used to illustrate each method. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current limitations, including the difficulty of separating overlapping mesh harmonics when the number of planet gears changes the sideband spacing, and directions for combining physics-based models with data-driven approaches.

SYN-PUB-00583.title: Comparison of empirical mode decomposition and wavelet packet transform for gearbox fault feature extraction
SYN-PUB-00583.text:
Comparison of empirical mode decomposition and wavelet packet transform for gearbox fault feature extraction (2015, conference, Proceedings of the 8th International Conference on Condition Monitoring and Machinery Failure Prevention Technologies (CMFPT), Novi Sad).
Authors: Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Ana Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: empirical mode decomposition; wavelet packet transform; gearbox diagnostics; feature extraction; k-nearest neighbour.
Gearbox tooth-surface fatigue and chipping faults produce non-stationary vibration signatures that challenge classical Fourier-based methods. This study compares empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and wavelet packet transform (WPT) for extracting fault-sensitive features from a two-stage helical gearbox test rig running at 1450 RPM under three load levels. Fourteen statistical features — including kurtosis, RMS, and energy ratio per sub-band — were computed from the intrinsic mode functions and wavelet packet nodes, respectively. A k-nearest neighbour classifier was trained and tested using stratified five-fold cross-validation on a dataset of 600 labelled acquisitions spanning healthy, pitting, and chipped-tooth conditions. WPT with a Daubechies-8 mother wavelet achieved 93.5% overall accuracy versus 87.2% for EMD-derived features, with the energy ratio from the third-level WPT nodes providing the most discriminative single feature. Misclassification was concentrated at low-load conditions for both methods.

SYN-PUB-00584.title: Vibration-based bearing fault classification using support vector machines with RBF kernels on a low-cost MEMS accelerometer platform
SYN-PUB-00584.text:
Vibration-based bearing fault classification using support vector machines with RBF kernels on a low-cost MEMS accelerometer platform (2017, journal, Measurement Science and Engineering Letters).
Authors: Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Tamás Kovács (outside co-author); Zoltán Varga (outside co-author); Nikola Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: MEMS accelerometer; support vector machine; bearing classification; low-cost sensing; frequency-domain features.
Industrial deployment of bearing diagnostics requires sensor and computation costs compatible with high-volume machinery. This paper evaluates a MEMS accelerometer (±16 g, 12-bit ADC, 10 kHz bandwidth) as an alternative to laboratory-grade piezoelectric sensors for classifying four bearing conditions: healthy, inner-race fault, outer-race fault, and rolling-element fault. A support vector machine with radial basis function kernel was trained on time-domain and frequency-domain features extracted from 1024-sample windows. Training data were collected at 1200 and 1800 RPM; test data included a 900 RPM speed not seen during training. Classification accuracy on the MEMS sensor reached 89.1% overall, compared with 95.4% for a co-located piezoelectric reference sensor. The accuracy gap was largest for rolling-element faults (−9.3 pp) due to the MEMS unit's higher noise floor above 4 kHz. Practical thresholds for minimum defect size detectable by the MEMS sensor are quantified.

SYN-PUB-00585.title: On-edge bearing fault detection with a convolutional neural network quantised for ARM Cortex-M4 deployment
SYN-PUB-00585.text:
On-edge bearing fault detection with a convolutional neural network quantised for ARM Cortex-M4 deployment (2019, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Embedded Computing).
Authors: Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Nikola Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: 1D-CNN; embedded inference; quantisation; microcontroller; bearing diagnostics.
Running inference for bearing diagnostics directly on a microcontroller eliminates the need for continuous data streaming to a central server, reducing latency and communication overhead. A one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) was designed to classify five bearing conditions from raw vibration windows of 2048 samples acquired at 25.6 kHz. The network was trained on 4800 labelled windows collected on a laboratory test rig, then quantised from 32-bit float to 8-bit integer using post-training quantisation. The resulting model (63 kB) was deployed on an STM32F4-based board. Inference time was 14.7 ms per window, and classification accuracy dropped by 1.8 percentage points compared with the floating-point baseline (94.6% versus 96.4%). Power draw during inference was measured at 38 mW. The study also reports sensitivity of accuracy to quantisation bit-width, showing that 8-bit suffices while 4-bit degrades performance by more than 6 pp.

SYN-PUB-00586.title: Fault detection in permanent-magnet synchronous motor bearings using combined vibration and stator current signals
SYN-PUB-00586.text:
Fault detection in permanent-magnet synchronous motor bearings using combined vibration and stator current signals (2020, journal, Diagnostics and Reliability in Rotating Systems).
Authors: Stefan Rădulescu (outside co-author); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Bogdan Bajić (R0045).
Keywords: sensor fusion; stator current; PMSM; bearing fault; random forest.
Vibration and stator current signals carry complementary information about bearing health in permanent-magnet synchronous motors. This study investigates sensor fusion of these two modalities for detecting outer-race and inner-race bearing faults at incipient and developed stages in a 2.2 kW PMSM under 25%, 50%, and 75% rated load. Features were extracted separately from each modality — RMS, kurtosis, and characteristic frequency amplitudes from vibration; sideband amplitudes around the supply frequency from current — and fused at the feature level before input to a random forest classifier. Fusion improved overall accuracy to 91.8% compared with 84.3% for vibration alone and 79.6% for current alone on a 480-sample test set. Gain was most pronounced at 25% load where vibration signal-to-noise ratio is lowest. The approach requires only a single additional current sensor if a vibration sensor is already present.

SYN-PUB-00588.title: Transfer learning for bearing fault detection across different machine configurations using domain adaptation
SYN-PUB-00588.text:
Transfer learning for bearing fault detection across different machine configurations using domain adaptation (2022, conference, Proceedings of the 14th European Conference on Structural Dynamics and Condition Monitoring (ECSDCM), Vienna).
Authors: Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Jana Turčanová (R0463); Dijana Čakarević (outside co-author); Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: transfer learning; domain adaptation; MMD; bearing fault; cross-machine.
Machine learning models trained on one rotating machine configuration frequently perform poorly when applied to a different machine with different nominal vibration characteristics. This paper evaluates maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) domain adaptation for transferring a bearing fault classifier trained on a 4-pole induction motor test rig to two target machines: a 6-pole motor and a belt-driven spindle, both with different bearing types. Source-domain training used 3200 labelled samples; target domains provided 0, 10, and 50 labelled samples in three adaptation scenarios. With zero target labels, MMD adaptation improved accuracy from 61.4% (no adaptation) to 76.9% on the 6-pole target and from 54.1% to 70.3% on the spindle. With 50 target labels, accuracy reached 88.2% and 83.7% respectively. Results suggest that moderate unlabelled target data is sufficient for useful transfer when vibration frequency bands are partially overlapping.

SYN-PUB-00589.title: Wireless sensor node with adaptive sampling for continuous bearing condition monitoring in multi-machine installations
SYN-PUB-00589.text:
Wireless sensor node with adaptive sampling for continuous bearing condition monitoring in multi-machine installations (2023, journal, Mechanical Systems Monitoring and Control).
Authors: Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Aleksandar Bogdanović (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author).
Keywords: wireless sensor node; adaptive sampling; IoT; field deployment; energy efficiency.
Continuous high-rate vibration sampling across many machines is energetically and bandwidth-intensive. This paper presents a wireless sensor node design in which the sampling rate adapts between a low-power survey mode (1 kHz, 5 s per minute) and a full-rate diagnostic mode (25.6 kHz, triggered) based on a lightweight RMS threshold computed on-chip. The node uses a sub-GHz radio and a primary lithium battery. Field deployment covered eight conveyor-drive bearings in a food processing facility over 14 months. Battery life exceeded 18 months at the observed trigger rate. Three developing bearing faults were flagged by the node and confirmed by scheduled inspection, with lead times of 19, 31, and 44 days before audible symptoms appeared. One false positive occurred, attributable to a temporary increase in ambient floor vibration during facility maintenance.

SYN-PUB-00590.title: Explainability of CNN-based bearing fault classifiers through gradient-weighted activation mapping on time-frequency inputs
SYN-PUB-00590.text:
Explainability of CNN-based bearing fault classifiers through gradient-weighted activation mapping on time-frequency inputs (2025, journal, International Journal of Condition Monitoring and Engineering).
Authors: Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Dijana Čakarević (outside co-author); Stefan Jakovljević (R0293); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Marco Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: Grad-CAM; explainability; CNN; STFT spectrogram; bearing fault.
Black-box neural network classifiers are difficult to validate for safety-relevant maintenance decisions. This study applies gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) to a 2D-CNN trained on short-time Fourier transform spectrograms to identify which time-frequency regions drive fault-class predictions for inner-race, outer-race, and cage faults in angular-contact bearings. The model was trained on 5600 spectrograms and achieved 94.1% five-fold cross-validated accuracy. Grad-CAM heat maps were generated for 200 correctly and 18 incorrectly classified test samples. For inner-race faults, activation concentrated consistently at the ball-pass inner-race frequency harmonic band, in agreement with analytical fault-frequency predictions. Outer-race activations were more distributed, correlating with sidebands rather than the carrier frequency. Misclassified samples showed activation in noise-dominated low-frequency regions, providing a diagnostic indicator for uncertain predictions. The results support Grad-CAM as a practical sanity-check tool for maintenance engineers.

SYN-PUB-00592.title: Effect of ambient temperature variation on the long-term stability of robot kinematic calibration in uncontrolled workshop environments
SYN-PUB-00592.text:
Effect of ambient temperature variation on the long-term stability of robot kinematic calibration in uncontrolled workshop environments (2022, journal, International Journal of Machine Tools and Manufacture).
Authors: Vladimir Ivanović (R0851); Bojan Lazić (outside co-author); Erika Horváth (outside co-author); Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Andrea Krstić (R0521); Tamás Vörös (outside co-author).
Keywords: ambient temperature; calibration stability; workshop environment; long-term accuracy; recalibration interval.
Calibration of industrial robots is routinely performed in temperature-controlled metrology rooms, yet robots operate in workshops where ambient temperature may vary by 15°C or more across a day. This study quantifies the degradation in calibration validity caused by ambient temperature swings using field measurements from two robot installations in an automotive component workshop in Novi Sad over a 90-day monitoring period. A laser tracker and a network of 24 ambient and structural temperature sensors logged data at 15-minute intervals. Calibration accuracy, expressed as the deviation of measured TCP positions from commanded positions, degraded from an initial 0.15 mm RMS to 0.38 mm RMS on days with ambient swings exceeding 12°C. A correction lookup table indexed by ambient temperature reduced this drift to 0.17 mm without requiring a full recalibration pass. The study quantifies the recalibration interval as a function of allowable accuracy budget and expected ambient temperature range, providing practitioners with a dimensioning tool.

SYN-PUB-00593.title: Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearings: Training Data Requirements and Generalisation Across Operating Conditions
SYN-PUB-00593.text:
Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearings: Training Data Requirements and Generalisation Across Operating Conditions (2020, journal, Journal of Intelligent Maintenance Systems).
Authors: Milena Stojković (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author); Filip Knežević (R0278); Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: LSTM; remaining useful life; deep learning; bearing; generalisation.
Recurrent neural networks with long short-term memory (LSTM) cells have been proposed for RUL prediction, but their practical data requirements are rarely quantified rigorously. This paper examines how many run-to-failure sequences are needed to train a reliable LSTM model, and how well a model trained at one operating condition generalises to others, using a dataset of 68 bearing run-to-failure sequences recorded at two speeds (1,200 and 1,800 rpm) and two radial loads (4 kN and 6 kN). Networks were trained on subsets ranging from 5 to 50 sequences. With 20 or more training sequences, mean absolute percentage error in RUL prediction stabilised near 14.3% at the 50% consumed-life mark. Cross-condition generalisation degraded performance to 22–28% MAPE when the training and test operating conditions differed, but a simple linear scaling of the health index by rated load and speed partially recovered accuracy to 17.1%. The study provides practical guidance for maintenance engineers considering LSTM-based prognosis tools.

SYN-PUB-00594.title: Comparison of time-domain AE features for estimating remaining useful tool life in intermittent milling
SYN-PUB-00594.text:
Comparison of time-domain AE features for estimating remaining useful tool life in intermittent milling (2015, journal, Journal of Manufacturing Processes and Systems).
Authors: Goran Mirković (R0219); Srđan Bojić (outside co-author); Ivan Marković (R0840); Bogdan Bajić (R0045); Ákos Tóth (outside co-author).
Keywords: remaining useful life; time-domain features; support vector regression; intermittent milling; tool wear.
Intermittent milling introduces periodic AE bursts that complicate continuous wear tracking methods designed for steady-state cutting. This work evaluates seven time-domain features — RMS, variance, peak-to-peak amplitude, crest factor, kurtosis, skewness, and signal entropy — for their ability to estimate remaining useful tool life (RUL) during slot milling of X40CrMoV5-1 steel (50 HRC). Experiments were conducted on a Haas VF-2 at three feed-per-tooth levels (0.04, 0.07, 0.10 mm/tooth). Each of 18 tool runs was continued until VB exceeded 300 µm. Features were computed from 20 ms gating windows aligned to the cutting interval. A support vector regression model trained on six runs at each feed level achieved median RUL errors of 12.4% (0.04 mm/tooth) and 17.1% (0.10 mm/tooth), with entropy and kurtosis providing the highest individual predictive power. The study provides quantitative guidance for selecting time-domain features when frequency-domain analysis is computationally prohibitive.

SYN-PUB-00819.title: Bearing and Gear Fault Signatures in a Combined Drivetrain Assembly: Mutual Interference and Separation Strategies
SYN-PUB-00819.text:
Bearing and Gear Fault Signatures in a Combined Drivetrain Assembly: Mutual Interference and Separation Strategies (2020, journal, Journal of Mechanical Diagnostics and Reliability).
Authors: Nataša Pavlović (outside co-author); Stefan Weinberg (outside co-author); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Ljiljana Puzović (R0061); Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737).
Keywords: drivetrain; fault interference; independent component analysis; decision fusion; multi-fault diagnosis.
In practical drivetrains, bearings and gears are mechanically coupled, and their fault signatures co-exist in a single vibration channel. This study characterises the interference patterns between simultaneously active bearing and gear faults using a modular drivetrain test rig. Eleven fault combination scenarios were tested, including healthy baseline, isolated bearing fault, isolated gear fault, and eight bearing–gear fault combinations of varying severity. Blind source separation using independent component analysis (ICA) is applied to a four-accelerometer array, and the separated components are individually analysed with SES and CS2. For bearing-dominated combinations, ICA recovers bearing signature SNR within 2 dB of the isolated fault case in 9 of 11 scenarios. Gear-dominated combinations are harder to separate, with residual bearing energy leaking into the gear component at levels up to −14 dB. A decision-level fusion rule combining component-level probabilities is proposed and yields 89.7% correct joint diagnosis across all 11 scenarios and 60 repeated runs.

SYN-PUB-01851.title: Cyclostationary Decomposition of Bearing Signals: Separating Deterministic and Random Components at Varying Speed
SYN-PUB-01851.text:
Cyclostationary Decomposition of Bearing Signals: Separating Deterministic and Random Components at Varying Speed (2015, journal, Mechanical Systems and Diagnostics).
Authors: Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Jérôme Castelet (outside co-author); Aleksandar Vujić (outside co-author); Katarina Todić (R0141).
Keywords: cyclostationary analysis; angular resampling; inner-race fault; variable speed; ICS2.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-02480.title: Benchmarking Prognosis Models for Industrial Pump Bearings on a Common Multi-Site Dataset: Methodology and Preliminary Results
SYN-PUB-02480.text:
Benchmarking Prognosis Models for Industrial Pump Bearings on a Common Multi-Site Dataset: Methodology and Preliminary Results (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.XXXXX).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Milena Stojković (outside co-author); Konstantinos Alexiou (outside co-author); Ivan Marković (R0840); Goran Starčević (R0192); Petra Novotná (outside co-author); Ana Terzić (outside co-author); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: benchmarking; prognosis; pump bearing; Gaussian process; evaluation metrics.
Comparisons of remaining useful life prognosis methods in the literature are often confounded by differences in experimental setup, health index definition, and evaluation metrics. This preprint describes a benchmarking protocol and a preliminary dataset collected from 31 pump bearing run-to-failure experiments across three industrial sites, standardising data format, health index construction, train/test split rules, and evaluation metrics (MAPE, scoring function, and coverage of 90% prediction intervals). Seven prognosis approaches were evaluated: Wiener-process model, particle filter with empirical degradation model, LSTM network, temporal convolutional network, Gaussian process regression, random survival forest, and a simple exponential smoothing baseline. No single method dominated across all sites and failure modes. The Gaussian process regression and random survival forest models showed the most consistent performance, while LSTM achieved the lowest MAPE on two of three sites but the widest prediction intervals. The dataset and evaluation code are provided as supplementary material.

SYN-PUB-02957.title: Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Small Wind Turbines Using Gradient-Boosted Survival Models on Vibration and SCADA Data
SYN-PUB-02957.text:
Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Small Wind Turbines Using Gradient-Boosted Survival Models on Vibration and SCADA Data (2024, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Predictive Maintenance in Energy Infrastructure (EWPMEI)).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Srđan Kovačević (outside co-author); Petra Horáková (outside co-author); Milica Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: survival analysis; wind turbine; vibration; SCADA; maintenance scheduling.
Small wind turbines installed on agricultural and industrial premises in Serbia are often maintained reactively due to the absence of dedicated condition monitoring. This paper fits gradient-boosted survival models—specifically, a discrete-time hazard model and a random survival forest—to a combined dataset of SCADA telemetry and tower-mounted accelerometer readings from 17 turbines over five years. Predictors include nacelle vibration root-mean-square in three frequency bands, rotor speed deviation, and nacelle temperature differential. The discrete-time hazard model achieved a concordance index of 0.73 on a held-out cohort, outperforming a Cox baseline at 0.65. Predicted 30-day failure probability was used to generate ranked maintenance schedules, which were evaluated in a retrospective simulation against actual maintenance logs, showing an estimated 22 % reduction in unscheduled downtime hours.

SYN-PUB-03481.title: A four-wire-rope passive isolation platform for a machine-vision camera on a milling machine table: design, analysis and bench test
SYN-PUB-03481.text:
A four-wire-rope passive isolation platform for a machine-vision camera on a milling machine table: design, analysis and bench test (2024, journal, Mechatronics and Precision Engineering).
Authors: Filip Knežević (R0278); Dušan Vlaisavljević (R0615); Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Milena Đorđević (outside co-author); Radu Constantin (outside co-author).
Keywords: passive isolation platform; machine-vision; wire-rope isolator; lumped-parameter model; CNC machine.
Machine-vision cameras co-located with CNC milling machines must tolerate spindle-frequency vibrations that can blur images and introduce measurement errors. This paper describes the mechanical design and experimental validation of a compact passive isolation platform sized to carry a 3.2 kg area-scan camera. The platform uses four identical 6 mm wire-rope isolators arranged symmetrically at the corners of an aluminium base plate. A lumped-parameter model with six degrees of freedom was assembled and its natural frequencies predicted analytically; the lowest mode was placed at 11 Hz to provide at least 20 dB isolation above 35 Hz. The assembled platform was tested on a laboratory shaker with representative spindle harmonics at 25 Hz, 50 Hz, and 75 Hz. Measured isolation ratios were 18 dB, 24 dB, and 31 dB at these frequencies, agreeing with model predictions to within 2 dB. Image blur was quantified using a resolution target: MTF50 improved from 38 lp/mm on the bare machine table to 61 lp/mm on the isolated platform under 50 Hz excitation at 12 mg input amplitude.

SYN-PUB-03662.title: Sensitivity of torsional dynamics simulations to damping model choice in early-pitting planetary gearbox scenarios
SYN-PUB-03662.text:
Sensitivity of torsional dynamics simulations to damping model choice in early-pitting planetary gearbox scenarios (2025, journal, Journal of Sound and Vibration Modelling).
Authors: Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Tatjana Ranđelović (outside co-author); Petra Horáková (outside co-author); Stefan Kovačević (outside co-author); Andrea Kuzmanović (R0506); Stefan Jakovljević (R0293).
Keywords: damping model; torsional simulation; sensitivity analysis; hysteretic damping; pitting severity.
The choice of damping model in multi-body torsional simulations of planetary gearboxes is examined for its effect on predicted vibration signatures when small pitting defects are present. Four damping models are compared: constant viscous mesh damping, load-dependent viscous damping, Rayleigh proportional damping, and a hysteretic damping formulation. Simulations are performed for a 3-planet gearbox at carrier speeds of 200, 400, and 800 rpm with sun gear pitting areas of 1, 3, 6, and 10 mm². The pitting severity index and its standard deviation over 50 simulated revolutions are used as comparison metrics. Hysteretic damping produces PSI values closest to experimental measurements from the department test rig, with a mean absolute error of 7.3% versus 14–22% for the other models. The sensitivity is most pronounced at low carrier speeds and small pit areas, where the difference between damping models in the PSI can reach 31%. Practical guidance for model selection based on available damping characterisation data is provided.

SYN-PUB-04384.title: Comparison of gear-mesh frequency extraction methods for planetary gearboxes under non-stationary load
SYN-PUB-04384.text:
Comparison of gear-mesh frequency extraction methods for planetary gearboxes under non-stationary load (2019, journal, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing — Regional Supplement).
Authors: Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Darko Ninkov (R0356); Petra Horáková (outside co-author); Jovana Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: non-stationary load; synchrosqueezed wavelet; Hilbert–Huang transform; mesh frequency tracking; wind turbine gearbox.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-05517.title: Torsional vibration decomposition in a two-stage helical gearbox using adaptive notch filtering
SYN-PUB-05517.text:
Torsional vibration decomposition in a two-stage helical gearbox using adaptive notch filtering (2013, journal, Journal of Machine Dynamics and Diagnostics).
Authors: Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Dragan Milosević (outside co-author); Jana Turčanová (R0463); Nemanja Vučić (outside co-author); Ksenija Ranković (R0602).
Keywords: adaptive notch filtering; torsional vibration; helical gearbox; side-band energy; residual signal.
This paper presents an adaptive notch filtering approach for isolating torsional vibration components in a two-stage helical gearbox operating under steady-state conditions. Measurements were taken on a 7.5 kW test rig at shaft speeds ranging from 600 to 1800 rpm using piezoelectric accelerometers and a non-contact torque sensor. The adaptive notch filter was tuned iteratively to suppress the fundamental gear-mesh frequency and its first three harmonics, yielding residual signals used for fault feature extraction. Side-band energy ratios were computed from the residual spectra and compared against a healthy baseline. Results showed that even at an early fabricated wear stage, the side-band energy ratio increased by a factor of 2.3 relative to the healthy condition. The method was benchmarked against synchronous averaging and cepstrum pre-whitening on the same dataset. Computational cost and filter convergence time are discussed for potential real-time deployment on embedded hardware with limited processing resources.

SYN-PUB-05845.title: Fault Isolation in Multi-Stage Centrifugal Compressors Using Sparse Sensor Placement and Lasso Regression on Spectral Features
SYN-PUB-05845.text:
Fault Isolation in Multi-Stage Centrifugal Compressors Using Sparse Sensor Placement and Lasso Regression on Spectral Features (2019, journal, Mechanical Systems Condition Assessment).
Authors: Aleksandar Vuković (outside co-author); Marek Svoboda (outside co-author); Đorđe Marinković (outside co-author); Vladana Radić (R0822); Andrea Kuzmanović (R0506); Saša Kosanović (R0496).
Keywords: sensor placement; compressor diagnostics; Lasso regression; fault isolation; spectral features.
Centrifugal compressors in natural gas processing are monitored at multiple measurement points, but sensor infrastructure is expensive to retrofit. This paper addresses fault isolation using a reduced sensor set selected by a greedy algorithm that maximises fault-class separability while minimising sensor count. Spectral features from 12 candidate accelerometer positions were computed on data from a three-stage compressor test rig under five fault conditions: surge margin reduction, impeller blade wear, seal gas leakage, misalignment, and bearing outer-race damage. A Lasso logistic regression model identified 4 sensor positions sufficient for 88.7% correct fault isolation across 480 test cases, compared with 91.3% using all 12 positions. Installation cost savings are estimated at 38% relative to full instrumentation. Sensitivity analysis shows that the selected four positions remain effective across the tested operating range of 60–100% rated speed. The generalisation of the sensor selection to other compressor geometries is discussed as a limitation.

SYN-PUB-05995.title: Multi-body torsional dynamics model for pitting fault simulation in a planetary gearbox sun gear
SYN-PUB-05995.text:
Multi-body torsional dynamics model for pitting fault simulation in a planetary gearbox sun gear (2017, journal, Mechanism and Machine Theory — Advances in Gear Dynamics (Special Issue)).
Authors: Miroslav Kolar (outside co-author); Dragan Milosević (outside co-author); Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Tatjana Ranđelović (outside co-author).
Keywords: multi-body dynamics; torsional model; pitting simulation; sun gear; stiffness reduction.
A six-degree-of-freedom multi-body torsional dynamics model of a planetary gearbox is developed to simulate the vibrational signature of progressive pitting damage on the sun gear tooth flanks. Pitting is represented as a time-varying stiffness reduction localised to a fraction of the meshing period, with pit area parameterised from 0.5 mm² to 12 mm² based on measured pit geometries from accelerated fatigue tests on case-hardened 18CrNiMo7-6 steel gears. Equations of motion are integrated using a variable-step Runge–Kutta solver. Simulated acceleration signals are compared with measured signals from a physical gearbox with artificially introduced pitting. The model reproduces the characteristic amplitude modulation sidebands observed in measured spectra with a frequency error below 1.2% and an amplitude ratio error below 15% for the first four sidebands. The sensitivity of the model to damping ratio uncertainty is quantified through a parameter sweep, showing that a ±20% variation in mesh damping ratio affects sideband amplitude predictions by at most 9%.

SYN-PUB-05996.title: Pitting severity index based on weighted sideband summation around gear-mesh harmonics in planetary stages
SYN-PUB-05996.text:
Pitting severity index based on weighted sideband summation around gear-mesh harmonics in planetary stages (2020, journal, Journal of Condition Monitoring in Mechanical Engineering).
Authors: Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Tatjana Ranđelović (outside co-author); Spasoje Petrović (R0868); Goran Lazić (outside co-author).
Keywords: pitting severity index; sideband summation; gear-mesh harmonics; fault severity; conveyor drive.
A scalar pitting severity index (PSI) is defined as a weighted sum of sideband amplitudes around the first four gear-mesh harmonics, with weights derived empirically from the torsional dynamics model published by the same group in 2017. The index is validated on two physical planetary gearboxes: a laboratory unit run to controlled pitting failure under accelerated fatigue at 1.8 times rated torque, and a repaired unit from a field-returned industrial conveyor drive. Vibration data were collected at 65.5 kHz. The PSI increased monotonically with measured pit area in the laboratory unit, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.94 across 11 damage stages from healthy to 35 mm² total pit area. On the field unit, the PSI correctly ranked five gearboxes of differing service history relative to their disassembly condition grades assigned by a maintenance engineer. False alarm rate at a threshold set to three standard deviations above the healthy mean was 4% across a 48-hour continuous monitoring run.

SYN-PUB-05997.title: Effect of gear tooth profile errors on torsional dynamics and diagnostic index reliability in planetary gearboxes
SYN-PUB-05997.text:
Effect of gear tooth profile errors on torsional dynamics and diagnostic index reliability in planetary gearboxes (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Vibrations in Rotating Machinery, Vienna).
Authors: Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Miroslav Kolar (outside co-author); Vladimir Ivanović (R0851); Jovana Đorđević (outside co-author); Luka Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: profile error; manufacturing tolerance; Monte Carlo simulation; detection threshold; mesh stiffness.
Manufacturing tolerances in tooth profile geometry introduce systematic variations in mesh stiffness that can mask or mimic early-stage pitting signatures. This study uses coordinate measuring machine data from twelve planetary gear sets to characterise profile deviation distributions for ISO quality grades 6, 7, and 8. The measured deviations are introduced into the multi-body torsional dynamics model as deterministic stiffness perturbations. Monte Carlo simulation with 500 realisations per quality grade quantifies the spread in the pitting severity index under healthy conditions. For grade 8 gears, the healthy-state PSI variance is 2.4 times larger than for grade 6, reducing the effective detection margin for pitting areas below 5 mm². Recommendations are formulated for adjusting detection thresholds based on the nominal manufacturing quality grade of a given gearbox, which can be retrieved from component documentation without disassembly.

SYN-PUB-05998.title: Real-time pitting detection prototype using FPGA-based gear-mesh harmonic extraction on a planetary gearbox test rig
SYN-PUB-05998.text:
Real-time pitting detection prototype using FPGA-based gear-mesh harmonic extraction on a planetary gearbox test rig (2024, conference, Mechatronics and Embedded Systems in Industrial Applications — Proceedings of the MESA Conference, Ljubljana).
Authors: Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Stefan Kovačević (outside co-author); Luka Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: FPGA; real-time diagnostics; synchronous resampling; pitting detection; embedded monitoring.
A real-time condition monitoring prototype is described in which gear-mesh harmonic extraction and pitting severity index computation are implemented on an FPGA development board (Xilinx Kria KV260) connected directly to a 24-bit delta-sigma accelerometer. The harmonic extraction algorithm performs synchronous resampling using a phase-locked loop driven by an encoder pulse train, followed by a 1024-point FFT executed on-chip at a latency of 1.1 ms per shaft revolution. The computed PSI is streamed over Ethernet to a monitoring dashboard at 10 Hz update rate. The prototype was tested on the department's planetary gearbox test rig with three implanted pitting fault levels (2 mm², 8 mm², and 20 mm² total pit area). Detection latency from fault presence to threshold crossing was below 4 shaft revolutions at all tested speeds between 300 and 900 rpm carrier speed. Power consumption of the FPGA module was 4.2 W during continuous operation.

SYN-PUB-05999.title: Threshold setting strategies for gear-mesh harmonic diagnostic indices under varying operating conditions: a survey of methods and a comparative study
SYN-PUB-05999.text:
Threshold setting strategies for gear-mesh harmonic diagnostic indices under varying operating conditions: a survey of methods and a comparative study (2026, preprint, arXiv / engrXiv (preprint, under review at Measurement Science and Engineering)).
Authors: Jovana Đorđević (outside co-author); Spasoje Petrović (R0868); Ivan Marković (R0840); Olivera Ognjanov (R0510); Goran Lazić (outside co-author).
Keywords: threshold setting; false alarm rate; receiver operating characteristic; operating conditions; condition monitoring benchmark.
Diagnostic indices derived from gear-mesh harmonic spectra require operating-condition-dependent thresholds to maintain acceptable false alarm and missed detection rates. This preprint surveys twelve threshold-setting strategies reported in the literature between 2005 and 2025 and applies six of them to a common dataset collected on a planetary gearbox test rig under four load levels and three temperature conditions. Strategies include fixed statistical thresholds, sliding window percentile methods, Gaussian mixture model fitting, control chart approaches, and two machine learning classifiers trained on healthy-condition data. Performance is evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves and F1 scores for five pitting severity levels. No single strategy dominates across all conditions; fixed statistical thresholds show the highest false alarm rates at partial load, while the sliding window percentile method performs most consistently but requires a longer initialisation window. The dataset used in the study is made available as a supplementary file.

SYN-PUB-06127.title: Interpretable Health State Classification for Induction Motor Bearings Using Shapelet-Based Time-Series Features
SYN-PUB-06127.text:
Interpretable Health State Classification for Induction Motor Bearings Using Shapelet-Based Time-Series Features (2025, journal, Journal of Intelligent Maintenance Systems).
Authors: Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Jelena Matić (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: shapelets; interpretability; induction motor; bearing health state; time-series classification.
Black-box classifiers for bearing health state estimation are often difficult to validate for deployment in safety-relevant applications. This paper develops an interpretable classification approach based on time-series shapelets—short subsequences whose presence discriminates between health states—extracted from raw vibration waveforms recorded from induction motor bearings under four health states: healthy, early outer-race damage, advanced outer-race damage, and inner-race damage. Shapelet discovery was performed on a training set of 2,400 labelled 0.5-second waveforms. The five most discriminative shapelets achieved 91.3% five-fold cross-validation accuracy using a nearest-shapelet distance classifier. Each shapelet was linked back to physical signal morphology (impacts, modulation patterns) and confirmed by domain-expert inspection. Comparisons with a support vector machine operating on 24 handcrafted spectral features showed equivalent accuracy (91.8%) but the shapelet approach required no manual feature engineering. Shapelet visualisation is shown to facilitate explanation of individual classifications to maintenance technicians.

SYN-PUB-06241.title: Soiling Rate Estimation on Utility-Scale PV Panels via Piecewise Linear Segmentation of Cleaned Irradiance-Normalised Output
SYN-PUB-06241.text:
Soiling Rate Estimation on Utility-Scale PV Panels via Piecewise Linear Segmentation of Cleaned Irradiance-Normalised Output (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Photovoltaics and Energy Management (CEPEM)).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Marija Vučković (outside co-author); István Varga (R0532).
Keywords: soiling estimation; piecewise segmentation; PV; SCADA; Pannonian region.
Soiling of photovoltaic panels reduces energy yield in a gradual, weather-dependent manner that is difficult to separate from other sources of degradation. This study applies piecewise linear segmentation to daily cleaned irradiance-normalised DC output records from a 1.1 MWp park monitored over 27 months. Rain events identified in co-located meteorological station data were used as natural cleaning markers, enabling segment-wise soiling rate estimation. Rates ranged from 0.04 % to 0.31 % per day depending on season and prevailing wind direction, consistent with dust transport patterns documented for the Pannonian plain. The method requires no additional soiling sensors and can be applied retrospectively to existing SCADA archives. Comparison with a reference clean-string approach showed mean absolute error below 0.09 % per day, demonstrating suitability for operational use.

SYN-PUB-07256.title: Adaptive EWMA Charts for Monitoring Autocorrelated Process Outputs: Simulation Study and Factory Trial
SYN-PUB-07256.text:
Adaptive EWMA Charts for Monitoring Autocorrelated Process Outputs: Simulation Study and Factory Trial (2017, journal, Quality and Reliability Engineering International).
Authors: Nataša Jovanović (outside co-author); Christoph Wenzel (outside co-author); Nevena Bogićević (R0636); Marija Ognjanov (R0817); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: EWMA; autocorrelation; adaptive smoothing; PLC; process monitoring.
Autocorrelation in process outputs is common when sampling is faster than the process time constant. Standard EWMA charts applied to autocorrelated data produce elevated false-alarm rates. This paper proposes an adaptive EWMA scheme in which the smoothing parameter λ is updated at each time step using a gradient-descent rule that minimises the one-step-ahead prediction error over a forgetting-factor-weighted window of past residuals. The scheme is compared with three baselines—fixed-λ EWMA on raw observations, fixed-λ EWMA on residuals from a fitted ARIMA model, and a T² chart on ARIMA residuals—across an AR(1) process with ρ ∈ {0.3, 0.6, 0.9} and mean shifts of 0.5 to 2.5σ. The adaptive scheme matched or exceeded ARIMA-residual EWMA in all tested conditions and was substantially easier to implement in a production PLC environment. A six-week trial on a bottling line confirmed an 11% reduction in false alarms.

SYN-PUB-07722.title: Detecting Abrupt and Gradual Faults in Hydraulic Actuator Systems Using a Combined CUSUM–Autoencoder Approach
SYN-PUB-07722.text:
Detecting Abrupt and Gradual Faults in Hydraulic Actuator Systems Using a Combined CUSUM–Autoencoder Approach (2022, journal, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773); Radmila Jakovljević (R0687); Borivoj Stanković (outside co-author); Dunja Vojnović (R1002).
Keywords: hydraulic actuators; CUSUM; autoencoder; fault detection; gradual drift.
Hydraulic actuator faults manifest as either abrupt jumps in pressure or flow or as gradual drift in actuator efficiency. Standard CUSUM charts detect the former reliably but respond slowly to the latter, while autoencoder reconstruction error captures complex multivariate deviations but is insensitive to the direction of change. This paper proposes a two-stage detector: a shallow convolutional autoencoder generates a residual vector, and a sign-constrained CUSUM statistic accumulates this residual in the direction identified by an offline fault-mode analysis. The combined statistic is evaluated on the public Hydraulic System Condition dataset (2 205 cycles, 17 sensors, four fault types) and on a laboratory actuator testbed. For gradual efficiency-loss faults, the combined scheme reduced mean detection delay from 41 cycles (autoencoder alone) to 17 cycles at a matched false-alarm rate of 1%. No improvement over plain CUSUM was observed for abrupt pressure-drop faults, confirming complementary strengths.

SYN-PUB-08170.title: Envelope Spectrum Indicators for Early Detection of Outer-Race Defects in Deep-Groove Ball Bearings Under Varying Radial Load
SYN-PUB-08170.text:
Envelope Spectrum Indicators for Early Detection of Outer-Race Defects in Deep-Groove Ball Bearings Under Varying Radial Load (2011, journal, Journal of Vibration and Condition Monitoring).
Authors: Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Srđan Tomić (outside co-author).
Keywords: envelope spectrum; BPFO; ball bearing; radial load; kurtosis.
This paper examines the sensitivity of squared envelope spectrum (SES) amplitude at bearing defect frequencies as a function of radial load in deep-groove ball bearings of type 6206. Accelerometer signals were recorded on a purpose-built test rig at shaft speeds of 600–1800 rpm and radial loads of 200–1200 N, with seeded outer-race defects of three severity levels (0.2, 0.5, 1.0 mm slot width). A total of 540 test runs were analysed. Results show that SES amplitude at BPFO and its first three harmonics increases monotonically with load and defect width, but that signal-to-noise ratio peaks near 800 N before degrading at higher loads due to structural resonance shifts. Crest factor and kurtosis are compared as alternative scalar indicators; kurtosis outperforms crest factor for the smallest defect class but saturates faster as severity increases. Threshold values derived from the healthy baseline allow correct binary classification in 94.6% of test cases using a fixed decision rule.

SYN-PUB-08171.title: Cepstral Lift-Off for Removal of Transmission Path Effects in Gearbox Vibration Spectra
SYN-PUB-08171.text:
Cepstral Lift-Off for Removal of Transmission Path Effects in Gearbox Vibration Spectra (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 6th Central European Symposium on Machinery Diagnostics, Brno).
Authors: Miroslav Radić (outside co-author); Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author).
Keywords: cepstral pre-whitening; gearbox; sideband level index; transmission path; gear mesh.
Gearbox vibration measurements are corrupted by the frequency response of the structural path between gear mesh and sensor mounting point. This study applies cepstral pre-whitening—log-spectral subtraction of the smoothed log-spectrum—to signals acquired from a two-stage helical gearbox test rig at the University of Novi Sad. Measurements were made at four torque levels (25, 50, 75, 100% rated) and three shaft speeds (900, 1200, 1500 rpm), producing 36 operating conditions. Gear mesh harmonics and their sidebands were compared before and after cepstral processing. After lift-off, the ratio of sideband amplitude to mesh harmonic amplitude increases by an average factor of 3.2 across all conditions, improving the visibility of localised tooth-fault sidebands. A subsequent sideband-level index (SLI) computed from the whitened spectrum correctly identifies the faulted gear in 91 of 96 repeated test runs. The method is computationally inexpensive and suitable for online implementation on standard industrial hardware.

SYN-PUB-08172.title: Multi-Class Fault Discrimination in Rolling-Element Bearings Using Random Forest on Envelope Spectrum Features
SYN-PUB-08172.text:
Multi-Class Fault Discrimination in Rolling-Element Bearings Using Random Forest on Envelope Spectrum Features (2017, journal, Journal of Mechanical Diagnostics and Reliability).
Authors: Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Nataša Pavlović (outside co-author); Bojan Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: random forest; multi-class classification; envelope spectrum features; rolling-element bearing; spectral kurtosis.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-08173.title: Condition Monitoring of Wind Turbine Main Bearings: Field Measurements and Spectral Trending Over 18 Months
SYN-PUB-08173.text:
Condition Monitoring of Wind Turbine Main Bearings: Field Measurements and Spectral Trending Over 18 Months (2018, conference, Wind Energy Systems and Technology Conference, Novi Sad).
Authors: Ivan Petrović (outside co-author); Milena Stojanović (outside co-author); Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737).
Keywords: wind turbine; main bearing; field measurement; spectral trending; outer-race spall.
This paper reports field vibration measurements from the main shaft bearing of a 850 kW horizontal-axis wind turbine located in Vojvodina, Serbia. Accelerometers and tachometers were installed on the main bearing housing, and data were collected at 10-minute intervals over 18 months using a ruggedised data acquisition unit. A total of approximately 78 000 spectral records were accumulated. Trending of SES amplitude at BPFO showed a gradual increase beginning in month 11, confirmed by lubricant debris analysis at month 13. The turbine was taken offline at month 16 for planned maintenance; inspection revealed a 2 mm spall on the outer race. Comparison of the vibration trend against manufacturer alarm thresholds shows the SES indicator preceded the threshold trigger by approximately six weeks, suggesting potential for earlier planned intervention. The study also characterises wind-speed-dependent noise floors, which must be normalised before trend comparison.

SYN-PUB-08174.title: Physics-Informed Feature Engineering for Gear Fault Classification: Embedding Kinematic Constraints into a Support Vector Machine
SYN-PUB-08174.text:
Physics-Informed Feature Engineering for Gear Fault Classification: Embedding Kinematic Constraints into a Support Vector Machine (2019, journal, Applied Mechanical Diagnostics).
Authors: Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Radovan Krstić (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: support vector machine; gear fault; physics-informed features; kinematic constraints; gearbox.
Standard machine learning classifiers applied to gearbox vibration data treat feature vectors as purely empirical.
