This work proposes a feature construction strategy that encodes kinematic gear mesh relationships explicitly: features are defined as amplitude ratios at theoretically predicted mesh harmonics and sidebands, with sideband spacing set equal to the shaft frequency of the potentially faulted wheel. This hard-wires gear geometry into the classifier input space. A support vector machine with RBF kernel is trained on 720 labelled segments from a two-stage helical gearbox at four fault conditions (healthy, pinion tooth chip, wheel tooth crack, backlash increase) plus five operating points. Classification accuracy is 93.8% versus 88.1% for a baseline SVM using raw spectral bins as features. The physics-informed approach also improves generalisation to a second, geometrically different gearbox with only 60 additional labelled samples for fine-tuning. The method does not require differentiable physics models and adds negligible computational overhead.

SYN-PUB-08175.title: Transfer Learning for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Across Different Machine Sizes Using Domain-Adversarial Training
SYN-PUB-08175.text:
Transfer Learning for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Across Different Machine Sizes Using Domain-Adversarial Training (2021, journal, Mechanical Systems and Diagnostics).
Authors: Ljiljana Vujović (outside co-author); Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Cosmin Dănilă (outside co-author).
Keywords: transfer learning; domain adaptation; bearing fault; domain-adversarial neural network; machine size variation.
Fault classifiers trained on laboratory-scale test rigs often fail when deployed on larger industrial machines due to domain shift in the vibration signal statistics. This paper evaluates domain-adversarial neural networks (DANN) as a transfer learning strategy for bearing fault diagnosis across three machines of different shaft diameter (25, 50, and 80 mm) with nominally equivalent bearing types. Source-domain training data comprised 4 800 labelled segments from the 25 mm rig; target domains had 0, 10, or 50 labelled target samples available. With zero target labels, DANN achieves 78.4% accuracy on the 80 mm machine versus 54.2% for a non-adapted baseline. With 50 labelled target samples, accuracy rises to 91.6%. Gradient reversal layer weight scheduling is shown to be a critical hyperparameter; a cosine annealing schedule outperforms fixed weighting by 3–5 percentage points. The study uses publicly shared feature extraction code and a dataset deposited in the institutional repository of the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

SYN-PUB-08176.title: Sparse Autoencoder Representations of Bearing Vibration for Anomaly Detection Without Fault Labels
SYN-PUB-08176.text:
Sparse Autoencoder Representations of Bearing Vibration for Anomaly Detection Without Fault Labels (2022, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Rotating Machinery Condition Monitoring, Split).
Authors: Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Miloš Janković (outside co-author); Ivana Mészáros (outside co-author).
Keywords: sparse autoencoder; anomaly detection; unsupervised learning; reconstruction error; embedded deployment.
Labelled fault data are expensive to acquire; this study explores unsupervised anomaly detection using a sparse autoencoder (SAE) trained exclusively on healthy bearing vibration. The SAE learns a compressed representation of 128-point mel-frequency spectral coefficient vectors. At inference, reconstruction error serves as an anomaly score. Experiments cover 6206 and 6308 bearing types, three fault modes, and two severity levels on the FTS rig. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) for anomaly detection across all fault types is 0.943 for the SAE against baselines of kurtosis (AUC 0.871) and RMS (AUC 0.784). Early detection threshold analysis shows that the SAE flags inner-race defects at 0.2 mm severity with a false-alarm rate of 4.3%, while kurtosis achieves the same false-alarm rate only at 0.5 mm severity. The autoencoder is compact (12 200 parameters) and executes in under 2 ms on a Raspberry Pi 4 single-board computer, demonstrating feasibility for low-cost embedded deployment.

SYN-PUB-08177.title: Gear Wear Progression Monitoring Using Time-Averaged Residual Signals and Wear-Rate Indicators
SYN-PUB-08177.text:
Gear Wear Progression Monitoring Using Time-Averaged Residual Signals and Wear-Rate Indicators (2023, journal, Applied Mechanical Diagnostics).
Authors: Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Radovan Krstić (outside co-author); Florin Muscă (outside co-author).
Keywords: gear wear; time-synchronous averaging; residual signal; wear-rate indicator; spur gear.
Progressive gear wear produces gradual changes in vibration that are less abrupt than tooth fracture and harder to track with threshold-based alarms. This paper presents a wear-rate indicator (WRI) derived from the time-synchronous average (TSA) residual signal—the TSA with all mesh harmonics and shaft-rate components removed. A controlled wear experiment was conducted over 240 hours of continuous operation on a spur gear pair (module 2, 40/80 tooth count) under 60 Nm torque. TSA residual RMS and the fourth statistical moment of the residual were recorded at four-hour intervals. Both indicators increase monotonically; WRI, defined as the slope of a linear fit to residual RMS over a 20-hour moving window, detects the onset of accelerated wear at hour 168, approximately 30 hours before the RMS crosses an absolute alarm threshold. Gear surface scans at 40-hour intervals correlate profile deviation (measured in µm) with WRI slope, confirming a linear relationship with R² = 0.91.

SYN-PUB-08178.title: Explainability of Convolutional Neural Network Fault Classifiers for Rotating Machinery: A Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping Study
SYN-PUB-08178.text:
Explainability of Convolutional Neural Network Fault Classifiers for Rotating Machinery: A Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping Study (2025, journal, Journal of Vibration and Condition Monitoring).
Authors: Gordana Kuzmanović (R0737); Ljiljana Vujović (outside co-author); Predrag Nikolić (outside co-author); Marta Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: convolutional neural network; Grad-CAM; explainability; fault classification; spectrogram.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on vibration spectrograms achieve high accuracy for bearing and gear fault diagnosis but provide limited insight into which time–frequency regions drive classification decisions. This paper applies Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) to a five-class CNN trained on short-time Fourier transform spectrograms from the FTS drivetrain test rig. The network achieves 95.1% accuracy on a held-out test set of 960 segments. Grad-CAM heat maps are compared against theoretically expected defect frequency bands for each class. For outer-race faults, peak activation aligns with BPFO ± 2 sidebands in 87% of correctly classified samples; for gear tooth-chip faults, activation aligns with the second and third mesh harmonic sideband clusters. Misclassified samples show activation spread across non-diagnostic frequency bands, suggesting data leakage from structural resonances. The analysis identifies two specific resonance windows (3.2–3.8 kHz and 6.1–6.7 kHz) that the network exploits spuriously, informing band-pass pre-filtering for improved generalisation.

SYN-PUB-08181.title: Baseline Performance Ratio Modelling for Grid-Connected PV Systems Using Ordinary Least Squares Regression on One-Year SCADA Logs
SYN-PUB-08181.text:
Baseline Performance Ratio Modelling for Grid-Connected PV Systems Using Ordinary Least Squares Regression on One-Year SCADA Logs (2014, journal, Journal of Renewable Energy Systems and Monitoring).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Marija Vučković (outside co-author); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: performance ratio; PV baseline; OLS regression; SCADA; degradation.
This paper presents a regression-based methodology for constructing performance ratio (PR) baselines for grid-connected photovoltaic installations using twelve months of five-minute SCADA records from a 2.4 MWp ground-mount park in Vojvodina. Ordinary least squares models were fitted separately for each inverter string, with irradiance, ambient temperature, and wind speed as predictors. The residual time series were then examined for systematic drift, which was taken as a proxy for gradual degradation. The fitted models explained between 91 % and 96 % of PR variance across sixteen inverter strings. A cross-validation scheme based on seasonal stratification was used to assess generalisation. Results showed that simple linear models are competitive with more complex approaches when training data cover at least eight months and include summer irradiance peaks. Limitations related to sensor calibration drift and curtailment events are discussed in detail.

SYN-PUB-08182.title: Early Fault Classification in Photovoltaic String Inverters Using Random Forest on SCADA-Derived Statistical Features
SYN-PUB-08182.text:
Early Fault Classification in Photovoltaic String Inverters Using Random Forest on SCADA-Derived Statistical Features (2018, journal, Journal of Industrial Condition Monitoring and Diagnostics).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Nemanja Petrović (outside co-author); Ágnes Kovács (outside co-author); Radovan Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: fault classification; random forest; string inverter; SCADA features; domain shift.
Inverter faults in distributed PV installations often produce subtle signatures in current and voltage telemetry before they result in full failure or protection trip. This paper extracts a set of 34 statistical features—including rolling mean, standard deviation, skewness, and crossing-rate measures—from five-minute SCADA records of eleven string inverters monitored over three years at two sites in Serbia. A random forest classifier trained on labelled fault events—covering IGBT degradation, grid relay issues, and sensor faults—achieved macro-averaged F1 of 0.81 on held-out data when a detection window of 48 hours before the logged fault event was used. Permutation importance analysis identified AC-side current imbalance and temperature-normalised efficiency drop as the two most informative features. The trained model was tested on a third site without retraining to assess domain shift, yielding an acceptable F1 of 0.73.

SYN-PUB-08183.title: Anomaly Scoring for District Heating Substation Telemetry Using Isolation Forest with Temporal Resampling
SYN-PUB-08183.text:
Anomaly Scoring for District Heating Substation Telemetry Using Isolation Forest with Temporal Resampling (2020, journal, Energy and Buildings Automation Journal).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Bojana Marković (outside co-author); Tomáš Novák (outside co-author).
Keywords: isolation forest; district heating; anomaly scoring; seasonal baseline; telemetry.
District heating substations generate continuous telemetry—supply and return temperatures, flow rate, differential pressure, valve position—that reflects both normal load variation and incipient faults. This paper applies isolation forest anomaly scoring to hourly-resampled records from 38 substations in a mid-sized Serbian city, covering two full heating seasons. To reduce the influence of strong daily and weekly periodicity, features were constructed as deviations from a Fourier-smoothed seasonal baseline rather than raw sensor values. Anomaly scores were validated against a maintenance log containing 54 confirmed fault events, yielding precision of 0.69 and recall of 0.78 at the chosen score threshold. False positives were predominantly associated with demand-side events such as building renovations. The paper also discusses operational considerations for deploying the pipeline in the control room of a heat utility, where interpretability requirements constrain model complexity.

SYN-PUB-08184.title: Comparison of Univariate and Multivariate LSTM Architectures for Remaining Useful Life Prediction in PV Inverters
SYN-PUB-08184.text:
Comparison of Univariate and Multivariate LSTM Architectures for Remaining Useful Life Prediction in PV Inverters (2021, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Workshop on Machine Learning in Energy Systems (BWMLES)).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Nemanja Petrović (outside co-author); Milica Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: LSTM; remaining useful life; PV inverter; attention mechanism; label noise.
Recurrent neural networks have been proposed for remaining useful life (RUL) estimation in power electronics, but the benefit of multivariate input over simpler univariate temperature-tracking models is not always clear in practice. This study compares four LSTM configurations—single-channel temperature, three-channel electrical, full nine-channel SCADA, and a multivariate model with attention—trained on labelled degradation sequences collected from 23 inverters across four sites over four years. RUL ground truth was derived from inverter replacement records. The univariate temperature model achieved mean absolute error of 18.3 days; the full nine-channel model with attention reduced this to 11.7 days. However, the improvement was statistically significant only for IGBT-related failures, not for capacitor or relay faults. Training data size, label noise from opportunistic rather than condition-triggered replacements, and class imbalance are examined as confounding factors.

SYN-PUB-08185.title: Transfer Learning for PV Fault Detection Across Geographically Distributed Sites with Different Inverter Brands
SYN-PUB-08185.text:
Transfer Learning for PV Fault Detection Across Geographically Distributed Sites with Different Inverter Brands (2022, journal, Renewable Energy Monitoring and Diagnostics).
Authors: Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author); Marija Vučković (outside co-author); Igor Starčević (R0738); Radovan Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: transfer learning; fault detection; PV; gradient boosting; cross-site generalisation.
Training fault detection models independently for each PV installation is data-expensive and impractical for small or newly commissioned sites. This paper investigates fine-tuning a source-domain random forest and a gradient-boosted tree, both pre-trained on five Serbian PV sites, using small labelled batches from two Romanian target sites with different inverter brands and monitoring intervals. Fine-tuning with as few as 30 labelled target-domain fault windows raised F1 from a zero-shot baseline of 0.48 to 0.74 for the random forest and to 0.77 for the gradient-boosted model. Feature alignment using quantile normalisation per sensor channel proved more effective than raw standardisation. The study uses publicly documented fault taxonomies and consistent labelling criteria to enable reproducibility, and the pre-trained model weights are made available with the paper.

SYN-PUB-08186.title: Threshold Selection Strategies for Operational Anomaly Detection Pipelines in Industrial SCADA Environments
SYN-PUB-08186.text:
Threshold Selection Strategies for Operational Anomaly Detection Pipelines in Industrial SCADA Environments (2023, journal, Journal of Industrial Data Science and Process Monitoring).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Ágnes Kovács (outside co-author).
Keywords: threshold selection; anomaly detection; SCADA; cost-sensitive; operational deployment.
Most anomaly detection research reports performance at a single fixed threshold chosen post-hoc to maximise a validation metric, which does not reflect operational reality where false alarm rates carry real costs. This paper surveys and empirically compares six threshold selection strategies—fixed percentile, precision–recall curve knee-point, F-beta optimisation, cost-sensitive selection, control-chart 3-sigma rule, and manual operator calibration—applied to isolation forest and autoencoder anomaly scores on SCADA telemetry from two PV parks and one wind farm. Data cover 36 months and 112 documented fault events. Cost-sensitive selection with an asymmetric cost matrix calibrated by an operator survey consistently outperformed fixed-percentile approaches across all three sites, reducing total operational cost by 19–34 % compared to the 95th-percentile baseline. The paper provides a decision workflow for practitioners choosing among strategies given available labelled data and operator input.

SYN-PUB-08187.title: Autoencoder-Based Detection of Sensor Drift in Long-Running PV Monitoring Systems
SYN-PUB-08187.text:
Autoencoder-Based Detection of Sensor Drift in Long-Running PV Monitoring Systems (2025, journal, Sensors and Instrumentation for Industrial Monitoring).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Nemanja Petrović (outside co-author); Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: autoencoder; sensor drift; PV monitoring; hardware-in-the-loop; reconstruction error.
Irradiance and temperature sensors deployed in field PV monitoring stations drift gradually due to soiling, ageing, and mechanical misalignment, introducing systematic bias into SCADA telemetry that is difficult to distinguish from true plant degradation. This paper trains a convolutional autoencoder on the first twelve months of records from twelve monitoring stations, treating this period as nominally calibrated, and then monitors reconstruction error on subsequent 36 months of data. Three types of drift—irradiance pyranometer zero-offset, temperature sensor gain shift, and voltage divider ageing—were induced artificially in a hardware-in-the-loop testbed to generate labelled validation data. The autoencoder flagged all three drift types within a two-week detection lag at an average false positive rate of 8 %. A lightweight rule-based filter using interquartile consistency across co-located sensors reduced false positives to 3 % without increasing the detection lag. The method was subsequently applied to two production archives where unconfirmed drift events were identified.

SYN-PUB-08188.title: Benchmarking Time-Series Foundation Models Against Classical Methods for Short-Horizon Anomaly Detection in Energy SCADA Telemetry
SYN-PUB-08188.text:
Benchmarking Time-Series Foundation Models Against Classical Methods for Short-Horizon Anomaly Detection in Energy SCADA Telemetry (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Srđan Kovačević (outside co-author); Bojana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: foundation models; benchmarking; anomaly detection; SCADA; edge deployment.
Large pre-trained time-series models have been proposed as general-purpose tools that can be applied to downstream tasks with little or no fine-tuning. This paper benchmarks three recently published time-series foundation models against four classical methods—isolation forest, one-class SVM, ARIMA residual scoring, and a simple rolling z-score—on anomaly detection tasks drawn from five SCADA datasets covering PV parks, a small wind farm, and district heating substations. Evaluation uses a consistent labelling protocol and the same six threshold selection strategies described in earlier work by the same group. Foundation models achieved the highest AUC-ROC on two of the five datasets but were outperformed by isolation forest on the remaining three, particularly where telemetry channels exhibit strong non-stationary seasonality. Inference latency and memory footprint are also reported, as they are relevant constraints for edge deployment in substation hardware.

SYN-PUB-08483.title: A Multivariate CUSUM Scheme with Adaptive Estimation of Covariance Structure for Batch Chemical Processes
SYN-PUB-08483.text:
A Multivariate CUSUM Scheme with Adaptive Estimation of Covariance Structure for Batch Chemical Processes (2010, journal, Journal of Quality Technology and Statistical Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Tatjana Lončar (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: CUSUM; adaptive covariance; batch processes; multivariate SPC.
Classical multivariate CUSUM charts assume a fixed in-control covariance matrix, an assumption routinely violated in batch manufacturing where operating conditions shift between phases. This paper proposes replacing the static covariance estimate with a sliding-window estimator updated at each sampling instant, with the window length selected by minimising a penalised prediction error over a rolling validation segment. The scheme was evaluated on a publicly available benchmark dataset from a simulated batch reactor (50 process variables, 1 000 batches) as well as on data collected from a plastics-extrusion line at a partner facility. On the benchmark, the average run length to detection for mean-shift magnitudes between 0.5 and 2.0 standard deviations improved by 18–34% compared with the fixed-covariance baseline, at the cost of a 7% increase in false-alarm rate. Parameter sensitivity, computational cost per sample, and the practical question of selecting the penalty coefficient are discussed in detail. The method is implemented in a freely available R package accompanying the paper.

SYN-PUB-08485.title: Online Detection of Covariance Shifts in Industrial Sensor Arrays Using the Generalised Likelihood Ratio Test
SYN-PUB-08485.text:
Online Detection of Covariance Shifts in Industrial Sensor Arrays Using the Generalised Likelihood Ratio Test (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Intelligent Systems and Informatics (SISY 2013)).
Authors: Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: covariance change detection; GLR test; sequential analysis; sensor arrays.
Changes in the covariance structure of a multivariate sensor stream can signal developing faults before any univariate indicator crosses a threshold. This paper applies a sequential generalised likelihood ratio (GLR) test to detect covariance shifts in an online, computationally efficient manner. The test statistic is computed over a sliding dual-window: a reference window of fixed length and a test window that grows until a detection is declared. Theoretical bounds on average run length are derived under a Wishart distribution model and confirmed by Monte Carlo simulation for dimensions p = 5, 10, 20 with 10 000 replicates each. The method is applied to a 14-channel temperature and pressure dataset from a district-heating substation, where it detected three confirmed maintenance events 40–120 seconds earlier than the plant's existing alarm system. Computational complexity is O(p²) per new sample after initial setup.

SYN-PUB-08486.title: Monitoring Nonlinear Process Dynamics with a Kernel Principal Component Analysis Control Chart: A Practical Assessment
SYN-PUB-08486.text:
Monitoring Nonlinear Process Dynamics with a Kernel Principal Component Analysis Control Chart: A Practical Assessment (2015, journal, Chemometrics and Process Analytics).
Authors: Branislava Ostojić (R0773); Aleksandar Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: kernel PCA; nonlinear SPC; Hotelling T²; fault detection.
Kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) projects nonlinear process data into a feature space where conventional Hotelling T² and Q statistics can be applied. Despite a substantial theoretical literature, practical guidance on kernel and hyperparameter selection for SPC purposes remains limited. This paper presents a systematic assessment of radial-basis-function and polynomial kernels across four industrial benchmark datasets (Tennessee Eastman process, simulated polymerisation reactor, rolling-mill dataset, and an in-house compressor dataset) using fault-detection rate and false-alarm rate as primary metrics. Cross-validation on in-control data was used to select the bandwidth parameter. Results show that RBF-KPCA outperforms linear PCA on three of four datasets, with the compressor data yielding the largest improvement (fault-detection rate 81% vs. 57% at a 1% false-alarm rate). The effect of the number of retained components is also analysed. An open-source Python implementation is included.

SYN-PUB-08487.title: Bayesian Change-Point Models for Multivariate Non-Stationary Time Series in Continuous Manufacturing
SYN-PUB-08487.text:
Bayesian Change-Point Models for Multivariate Non-Stationary Time Series in Continuous Manufacturing (2016, journal, Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation).
Authors: Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ilona Szabo (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: Bayesian change-point detection; BOCPD; Normal-Inverse-Wishart; continuous manufacturing.
Many continuous manufacturing processes operate under time-varying mean and variance due to raw-material variability and gradual equipment wear. Standard SPC methods tuned on historical data deteriorate in such environments. This paper formulates a Bayesian online change-point detection model (BOCPD) extended to multivariate observations under a Normal-Inverse-Wishart conjugate prior. The model simultaneously estimates the probability of a change and updates the predictive distribution after each new sample. Two variants are compared: one with a fixed hazard rate and one with a hazard rate estimated from past inter-change intervals using empirical Bayes. On simulated data with p = 8 variables, 500 change points, and signal-to-noise ratios between 0.5 and 3.0, the empirical-Bayes variant reduced the mean detection delay by 1.8 samples at a fixed false-alarm rate of 0.5%. The method was validated on accelerometer data from a CNC milling machine spindle over a six-month period.

SYN-PUB-08488.title: Unsupervised Segmentation of Industrial Time Series via a Penalised Piecewise-Stationary Model
SYN-PUB-08488.text:
Unsupervised Segmentation of Industrial Time Series via a Penalised Piecewise-Stationary Model (2018, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Borivoj Stanković (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: time series segmentation; piecewise stationarity; BIC; dynamic programming; cyber-physical systems.
Long industrial time series collected from cyber-physical systems rarely satisfy stationarity over their full length. This paper treats segmentation as a model-selection problem: a piecewise-stationary multivariate Gaussian model is fitted, and the number and positions of segments are chosen by minimising a modified BIC penalising both the number of segments and their minimum length. Optimisation uses a dynamic programming algorithm with complexity O(n²) in the number of observations. The approach is compared with binary segmentation and wild binary segmentation on 24 synthetic scenarios (varying segment lengths 50–500 and p = 4–16 variables) and on three industrial datasets: a paper-machine headbox, a wastewater treatment blower, and a refrigeration compressor. BIC-guided dynamic programming achieved the lowest mean absolute error in estimated change-point locations on 19 of 24 synthetic scenarios and recovered all manually labelled regime changes in the wastewater dataset.

SYN-PUB-08489.title: Statistical Process Control for Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey of Methods and Open Challenges
SYN-PUB-08489.text:
Statistical Process Control for Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey of Methods and Open Challenges (2019, book chapter, Handbook of Industrial Data Science (Edited Volume, Springer Academic Press)).
Authors: Branislava Ostojić (R0773); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Marta Reinhardt (outside co-author).
Keywords: SPC survey; cyber-physical systems; online learning; anomaly detection; benchmark.
Cyber-physical systems produce streams of heterogeneous sensor data at high sampling rates, creating both opportunities and difficulties for statistical process control. This chapter surveys methods applicable to the monitoring of such systems, organising them along four dimensions: the stationarity assumption (static vs. adaptive), the observation structure (univariate vs. multivariate), the supervision level (supervised vs. unsupervised), and the computational setting (batch vs. online). For each combination, representative methods are described and their assumptions, strengths, and computational requirements are tabulated. Special attention is given to the interaction between control-chart theory and machine-learning approaches, including isolation forest, autoencoders, and one-class SVMs as anomaly scorers whose output feeds threshold-based alarms. Open challenges discussed include distribution shift under normal ageing, alarm rationalisation in dense sensor networks, and the absence of labelled fault data. The chapter concludes with a set of benchmark recommendations for the community.

SYN-PUB-08490.title: One-Class SVM Anomaly Scores as Control-Chart Statistics: Calibration, Threshold Setting, and Recalibration Frequency
SYN-PUB-08490.text:
One-Class SVM Anomaly Scores as Control-Chart Statistics: Calibration, Threshold Setting, and Recalibration Frequency (2020, journal, Computers and Industrial Engineering).
Authors: Aleksandar Đorđević (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: one-class SVM; anomaly score calibration; control chart; drift detection; edge deployment.
One-class support vector machines produce a real-valued decision score that can serve as a univariate control-chart statistic, enabling the combination of nonlinear pattern recognition with the interpretability of run rules and average-run-length guarantees. This paper addresses three practical questions: (1) how to calibrate raw SVM scores to approximate a false-alarm probability, (2) how to set the control limit given a desired in-control ARL, and (3) how frequently the SVM must be retrained to maintain calibration when the in-control distribution drifts slowly. Using a Platt-scaling calibration step and a bootstrap-based limit-setting procedure, the method achieves in-control ARLs within 5% of nominal across six simulated drift scenarios. Recalibration triggered by a secondary drift-detection statistic on residuals reduced worst-case ARL inflation from 43% to 9% on a simulated six-month conveyor-belt dataset with gradual load increase. The paper reports training times and discusses feasibility for edge deployment.

SYN-PUB-08491.title: Federated Learning for Distributed Statistical Process Monitoring Across Multiple Production Lines
SYN-PUB-08491.text:
Federated Learning for Distributed Statistical Process Monitoring Across Multiple Production Lines (2021, journal, Journal of Manufacturing Systems).
Authors: Nataša Jovanović (outside co-author); Ilona Szabo (outside co-author); Stefan Gruber (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: federated learning; distributed SPC; anomaly detection; heterogeneous data; production monitoring.
When identical or similar machines operate at multiple plants, it is attractive to pool monitoring knowledge across sites without centralising raw sensor data for privacy or bandwidth reasons. This paper adapts federated averaging to train a shared anomaly-detection model for multivariate SPC, with each plant training locally on its own data and contributing model updates to a central aggregator. Four federated aggregation strategies are compared against a centralised baseline and a local-only baseline on a network of five simulated production lines with heterogeneous fault-type distributions. Federated averaging with client-side control-limit adjustment achieved fault-detection rates within 4 percentage points of the centralised model on three of five sites, while local-only models lagged by 11–19 percentage points. Communication overhead, convergence speed, and the influence of data heterogeneity on model drift are quantified. Limitations regarding non-IID client data are discussed.

SYN-PUB-08493.title: Benchmarking Change-Point Detection Algorithms on Annotated Industrial Datasets: Methodology and Initial Results
SYN-PUB-08493.text:
Benchmarking Change-Point Detection Algorithms on Annotated Industrial Datasets: Methodology and Initial Results (2024, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Data-Driven Process Control (DDPC 2024)).
Authors: Aleksandar Đorđević (outside co-author); Stefan Gruber (outside co-author); Vesna Todorović (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: change-point detection benchmark; PELT; BOCPD; evaluation methodology; annotated datasets.
Published evaluations of change-point detection algorithms are difficult to compare because they use different datasets, annotation conventions, and performance metrics. This paper proposes a reproducible benchmarking protocol and applies it to eight algorithms—including BOCPD, PELT, RUPTURES binary segmentation, wild binary segmentation, BOCD with student-t likelihood, L2-cost dynamic programming, a kernel change-point detector, and an LSTM-based method—on six annotated industrial datasets contributed by the authors and three collaborating groups. Annotations were produced by domain engineers and reviewed by a second engineer; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Metrics reported include F1 score at a tolerance of five samples, mean absolute error in change-point location, and computational time per 1 000 observations. No single algorithm dominated across all datasets. PELT performed best on datasets with large between-segment variance ratios, while the kernel method was most robust on datasets with covariance-only changes. The datasets and annotation files are deposited in a public repository.

SYN-PUB-08494.title: Monitoring Concept Drift in Online Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial IoT Streams
SYN-PUB-08494.text:
Monitoring Concept Drift in Online Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial IoT Streams (2025, journal, IEEE Internet of Things Journal).
Authors: Nataša Jovanović (outside co-author); Ilona Szabo (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: concept drift; isolation forest; Page–Hinkley test; Industrial IoT; incremental learning.
Anomaly detection models deployed in industrial IoT environments face concept drift: the statistical properties of normal operation change over months due to seasonal variation, equipment ageing, or production-mix changes. This paper proposes a two-level monitoring architecture in which a primary anomaly detector (isolation forest trained offline) is supervised by a secondary drift monitor based on the Page–Hinkley test applied to the score distribution's empirical mean and variance. When drift is confirmed, a lightweight incremental update procedure re-weights the forest using recent in-control samples without full retraining. The architecture is evaluated on 18 months of data from three IoT-connected air-compressor units at a manufacturing plant, comprising approximately 4.7 million observations per unit. The drift monitor correctly identified seven of eight documented operating-regime transitions with one false trigger. Post-update fault-detection rates recovered to within 3% of the initial model's performance within 2 000 samples of each transition.

SYN-PUB-08925.title: Envelope Spectrum Analysis for Early Bearing Fault Detection in Industrial Centrifugal Pumps
SYN-PUB-08925.text:
Envelope Spectrum Analysis for Early Bearing Fault Detection in Industrial Centrifugal Pumps (2010, journal, Journal of Vibration Diagnostics and Machinery Health).
Authors: Vladana Radić (R0822); Dragan Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: envelope spectrum; bearing fault; centrifugal pump; kurtosis; bandpass filter.
This paper examines the use of envelope spectrum analysis applied to accelerometer signals collected from the drive-end and non-drive-end bearings of three centrifugal pumps operating under variable load conditions in a food processing facility. Vibration data were recorded at 25.6 kHz over a six-month period, accumulating approximately 1,800 hours of run-time data per unit. Bandpass filter parameters were optimised using kurtosis maximisation across 48 sub-bands. The envelope spectra reliably identified outer-race defect frequencies at signal-to-noise ratios as low as 4 dB before any audible symptom appeared. Comparisons were made between healthy and seeded-fault bearings under three load levels (25%, 50%, 75% of rated capacity). Detection lead times ranged from 11 to 34 days ahead of functional failure, depending on load severity. The study provides practical filter-selection guidelines for practitioners without access to specialised diagnostic software, and discusses limitations imposed by variable shaft speed.

SYN-PUB-08926.title: Comparison of Time-Domain Statistical Features for Gearbox Fault Classification Under Non-Stationary Load
SYN-PUB-08926.text:
Comparison of Time-Domain Statistical Features for Gearbox Fault Classification Under Non-Stationary Load (2012, conference, Proceedings of the 10th International Conference on Condition Monitoring and Machinery Failure Prevention Technologies, Belgrade).
Authors: Milena Stojković (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: gearbox fault; statistical features; LDA; non-stationary load; classification.
A systematic comparison of eighteen time-domain statistical features—including RMS, crest factor, kurtosis, skewness, and several higher-order moments—is presented for the classification of four gearbox fault types: healthy, chipped tooth, missing tooth, and worn tooth. Experiments were conducted on a back-to-back gearbox test rig operating at shaft speeds between 600 and 1,800 rpm under stepwise torque profiles. Each condition was recorded over 30 independent trials of 60 seconds each. A linear discriminant analysis classifier was trained on 70% of trials and tested on 30%. Under stationary load, kurtosis and crest factor together achieved 94.2% classification accuracy. Under non-stationary load, accuracy degraded to 78.6% using the same feature set, with the most frequent confusion occurring between chipped and worn tooth conditions. The paper concludes with recommendations for feature normalisation strategies that partially recover accuracy under variable-speed operation.

SYN-PUB-08927.title: Simultaneous Vibration and Surface Temperature Monitoring of Rolling Element Bearings: Correlation and Complementarity
SYN-PUB-08927.text:
Simultaneous Vibration and Surface Temperature Monitoring of Rolling Element Bearings: Correlation and Complementarity (2013, journal, Journal of Vibration Diagnostics and Machinery Health).
Authors: Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Dragomir Jelić (outside co-author); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: infrared thermometry; multimodal monitoring; bearing failure; sensor fusion; lubrication fault.
Rolling element bearings in a 37 kW induction motor test stand were instrumented with both piezoelectric accelerometers and non-contact infrared thermometers to assess whether combining both signal modalities improves early fault detection compared with either modality alone. Four bearing failure modes were induced: outer-race spall, inner-race spall, ball defect, and lubrication starvation. Data were collected over 200-hour run-to-failure experiments for each condition. Correlation coefficients between vibration kurtosis and surface temperature rise were computed at 30-minute intervals. Temperature rise alone lagged vibration-based indicators by 6 to 18 hours depending on fault type. However, for lubrication starvation faults, thermal indicators reached statistically significant thresholds 4.2 hours earlier than vibration kurtosis. A simple fusion rule based on logical OR combination reduced missed detections from 12% to 3% across all fault types, with no increase in false alarm rate.

SYN-PUB-08928.title: Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Gearbox Bearings Using Particle Filter Prognosis
SYN-PUB-08928.text:
Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Gearbox Bearings Using Particle Filter Prognosis (2015, journal, Mechanical Systems Condition Assessment).
Authors: Vladana Radić (R0822); Milena Stojković (outside co-author); Aleksandar Vuković (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author).
Keywords: remaining useful life; particle filter; degradation model; run-to-failure; prognosis.
This work presents a particle filter framework for estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of gearbox output-shaft bearings. A state-space degradation model was constructed from experimental run-to-failure data obtained from 14 identical bearing specimens tested on an accelerated life test rig at 1,500 rpm and 110% of rated radial load. The RMS of the high-frequency band (8–16 kHz) served as the health index. Particle filter parameters—number of particles, process noise covariance, and measurement noise covariance—were tuned via cross-validation on six training runs. The model was evaluated on the remaining eight runs. Mean absolute error in RUL prediction at the 50% life-consumed point was 6.3 hours against a mean actual remaining life of 41.7 hours. Prediction uncertainty bounds narrowed progressively as fault progression advanced. The approach is compared with an extended Kalman filter baseline, which yielded a mean absolute error of 9.8 hours under the same evaluation protocol.

SYN-PUB-08929.title: Thermal Imaging-Based Condition Assessment of Slow-Speed Roller Bearings in Conveyor Systems
SYN-PUB-08929.text:
Thermal Imaging-Based Condition Assessment of Slow-Speed Roller Bearings in Conveyor Systems (2016, conference, Proceedings of the 4th South-East European Symposium on Industrial Maintenance, Novi Sad).
Authors: Đorđe Marinković (outside co-author); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: infrared thermography; slow-speed bearings; conveyor; thermal threshold; emissivity.
Slow-speed roller bearings (shaft speed 15–80 rpm) present particular challenges for vibration-based diagnostics because fault-related frequencies fall below 10 Hz and are easily masked by structural noise. This paper investigates whether infrared thermography can serve as a primary diagnostic tool in such applications. Fourteen roller bearings from operating conveyor systems in a Vojvodina grain handling facility were inspected quarterly over 18 months using a calibrated thermal camera with a 320×240 focal plane array and 0.05 °C thermal resolution. Temperature differentials between the bearing housing and ambient were logged alongside manually assessed visual condition grades. A threshold of 8 °C above ambient was found to coincide reliably with the onset of detectable surface pitting, while a 15 °C differential indicated advanced degradation requiring imminent replacement. The paper also discusses emissivity correction procedures for painted versus bare metal housings and quantifies the effect of ambient air movement on measurement repeatability.

SYN-PUB-08930.title: Multivariate Statistical Process Control for Simultaneous Monitoring of Multiple Bearing Locations in Rotating Machinery
SYN-PUB-08930.text:
Multivariate Statistical Process Control for Simultaneous Monitoring of Multiple Bearing Locations in Rotating Machinery (2017, journal, Journal of Industrial Measurement and Control Systems).
Authors: Milena Stojković (outside co-author); Iosif Drăghici (outside co-author); Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: PCA; Hotelling T²; multivariate SPC; gearbox; fault detection.
Industrial rotating machines are typically equipped with multiple bearing points whose health may degrade independently or in coupled fashion. This paper develops a multivariate statistical process control framework, based on Hotelling's T² and the Q-statistic derived from principal component analysis, applied simultaneously to vibration features extracted from four bearing positions on a two-stage gearbox test stand. Feature vectors comprising RMS, kurtosis, and spectral energy in four frequency bands were computed from 1-second data windows at 30-second intervals over 900 hours of monitored operation including 22 seeded fault events. The Hotelling T² chart detected 19 of the 22 events, with a mean detection lag of 1.4 hours and 2 false alarms during the healthy baseline period. The Q-statistic contributed complementary sensitivity for four events missed or delayed by T². The paper discusses the selection of the number of retained principal components and the impact of load variation on control limit stability.

SYN-PUB-08931.title: Transfer Learning for Bearing Fault Diagnosis When Source and Target Domains Differ in Machine Size and Speed
SYN-PUB-08931.text:
Transfer Learning for Bearing Fault Diagnosis When Source and Target Domains Differ in Machine Size and Speed (2021, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Rotating Machinery Diagnostics (EuroRoMaDi), Vienna).
Authors: Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Iosif Drăghici (outside co-author); Lukas Reindl (outside co-author); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: transfer learning; domain adaptation; CNN; bearing fault; industrial motor.
Labelled run-to-failure data from small laboratory test rigs are abundant, while equivalent data from large industrial machines are scarce. This paper investigates domain adaptation via fine-tuning of a convolutional neural network pre-trained on laboratory bearing data (shaft diameter 30 mm, 1,500 rpm) and applied to a 250 kW industrial motor (shaft diameter 100 mm, 750 rpm). The source dataset comprised 3,200 labelled one-second vibration windows across four fault classes; the target domain provided only 80 labelled windows per class for fine-tuning. Without adaptation, accuracy on the target domain was 61.4%. Fine-tuning the last two convolutional blocks on the small target dataset raised accuracy to 83.9%. Further improvement to 87.2% was obtained by including adversarial domain alignment of intermediate feature representations. The paper analyses which convolutional layers encode transferable versus domain-specific features, finding that the first two layers consistently transferred well regardless of machine size ratio.

SYN-PUB-08932.title: Edge-Deployable Anomaly Detection for Pump Monitoring Using Autoencoder Compression of Vibration Spectra
SYN-PUB-08932.text:
Edge-Deployable Anomaly Detection for Pump Monitoring Using Autoencoder Compression of Vibration Spectra (2022, journal, Journal of Industrial Measurement and Control Systems).
Authors: Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Vladana Radić (R0822); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: autoencoder; edge computing; anomaly detection; pump monitoring; embedded systems.
Deploying data-driven condition monitoring at the network edge requires models small enough to run on microcontroller-class hardware. This paper describes the design, training, and deployment of a sparse autoencoder that compresses 512-point FFT spectra from pump bearing accelerometers into 16-dimensional bottleneck representations. The autoencoder was trained exclusively on healthy operation data from six pumps over three months (approximately 4.7 million spectrum snapshots). Reconstruction error served as the anomaly score. The deployed model occupied 47 kB of flash memory on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller and executed inference in 2.3 ms per spectrum. Over a subsequent 14-month monitoring period covering three pump failures and one false alarm, the system detected all three failures between 8 and 31 days before shutdown, with a false alarm rate of 0.7 events per pump per year. Power consumption of the monitoring node averaged 210 mW, enabling battery-backed installation.
